question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool indicate at least a 25% probability of a 50+ basis point rate cut at the January 2026 FOMC meeting by October 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The CME FedWatch Tool tracks market expectations for Federal Reserve rate decisions based on futures pricing. Currently, following the September 17, 2025 rate cut of 25 basis points (to 4.00%-4.25%), market expectations are focused on gradual cuts. The CME FedWatch Tool showed a 93.2% probability of a 25bps cut at the October 2025 meeting and 92.7% for December 2025, but no specific probability was reported for a 50+ bps cut in January 2026. Market sentiment shifting toward expecting a larger cut (50+ bps) in January 2026 would be a strong indicator that economic conditions are deteriorating faster than anticipated, potentially prompting more aggressive Fed action.

Sources:
- CME Group FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
- Current Fed Funds Rate (4.00%-4.25%): https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the CME FedWatch Tool's 'Probability of 50+ bps Rate Cut' for the January 27-28, 2026 FOMC meeting reaches or exceeds 25% at any time between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-17 (inclusive), as recorded on the official CME FedWatch Tool page (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html). The probability must be clearly displayed for the January 2026 meeting. If the tool does not explicitly show probabilities for 50+ bps cuts, but shows probabilities for target rate ranges (e.g., 3.50-3.75% if current is 4.00-4.25%), then a probability ≥25% for a target range that implies a 50+ bps cut (e.g., 3.50-3.75% or lower) will also count as Yes. If the FedWatch Tool is unavailable or does not update during the resolution window, the question resolves based on the last available data before October 18, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: Market expectations for Fed rate cuts, as reflected in the CME FedWatch Tool, are a leading indicator of actual Fed policy decisions. A significant increase in the probability of a large (50+ bps) cut in January 2026 would signal that traders anticipate deteriorating economic conditions (e.g., rising unemployment or falling inflation) that could compel the Fed to act more aggressively. This subquestion provides early insight into whether the conditions for a large rate cut are emerging, which is directly relevant to the ultimate question about the Fed's action in January 2026.

question: Trump declassifies UFO files in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump administration declassifies any previously classified files pertaining to extraterrestrial life and/or unexplained arial phenomena by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Announcements of declassifications that are not implemented within this market's timeframe will not count.

The primary resolution source for declassification will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the US Initial Jobless Claims 4-week moving average exceed 250,000 at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Initial Jobless Claims are a leading indicator of labor market health and potential economic distress. A sustained increase in claims often precedes recessions as layoffs rise. The 4-week moving average smooths out weekly volatility and provides a clearer trend. As of August 2025, the 4-week moving average of Initial Jobless Claims was approximately 220,000 (based on recent trends). The 250,000 threshold represents a significant deterioration from current levels and would indicate worsening labor market conditions. Historically, claims above this level have often coincided with or preceded recessions.

Sources:
- U.S. Department of Labor: https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/UI/claims-data
- Federal Reserve Economic Data: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/IC4WSA
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the seasonally adjusted 4-week moving average of US Initial Jobless Claims, as reported by the U.S. Department of Labor in its weekly Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report, equals or exceeds 250,000 at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The official source is the Department of Labor's weekly report at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/UI/claims-data. If multiple reports show claims above this threshold during this period, the question resolves Yes. If the Department of Labor stops publishing this data during this period, the question will resolve based on the last available report. If the reporting methodology changes significantly, resolution will be based on the most comparable available metric.
subquestions.rationale: Rising jobless claims are a reliable leading indicator of economic distress and often precede recessions. A sharp increase to 250,000+ would signal deteriorating labor market conditions that could lead to reduced consumer spending and potentially trigger or confirm a recession. This provides an early warning signal for the 2025 recession question while being resolvable within the required timeframe.

question: Will Max Verstappen be the 2025 Drivers Champion?
description:
This market will resolve according to the driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2025 F1 season. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

As soon as the results for the final scheduled race of the 2025 F1 season are known this market will resolve.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2025 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), this market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

subquestions.question: Will Max Verstappen finish on the podium at the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix?
subquestions.background_information: The Singapore Grand Prix (October 3-5, 2025) is a crucial indicator of Red Bull's performance in high-downforce, hot conditions where they historically struggle. Verstappen has had mixed results at Singapore: he won in 2022 and 2023 but had a non-podium finish in 2023 due to car issues. Red Bull's recent performance improvements (winning Monza and Baku) suggest they may be competitive, but Singapore's high-downforce nature remains a challenge. Verstappen's current championship position (3rd, 69 points behind Piastri) means podium finishes are essential to keep his title hopes alive. A podium here would signal Red Bull's car is competitive across diverse circuits, while a non-podium would suggest persistent weaknesses. Sources: Motorsport.com analysis of Singapore as a benchmark (https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/after-baku-brilliance-here-s-why-singapore-gp-is-key-for-max-verstappen-s-f1-title-hopes/10645689/), Verstappen's Singapore history (F1 official stats: https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2023/races/1222/singapore/race-result.html).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Max Verstappen finishes in 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place in the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix race (October 5, 2025). The race result must be confirmed by the official FIA race classification published on Formula 1's official website (https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2025/races/). If the race is canceled, postponed beyond October 31, 2025, or results are not officially published, the question resolves to 'No' (as Verstappen cannot score podium points). Resolution window: October 1, 2025 (start) to October 5, 2025 (end, race date).
subquestions.rationale: Singapore is a high-downforce, hot circuit where Red Bull has historically struggled (Verstappen had a non-podium here in 2023). A podium finish would indicate Red Bull's recent improvements are genuine across all circuit types, boosting Verstappen's title chances. A non-podium suggests Red Bull's car remains inconsistent, making a 2025 title win less likely given Verstappen's 69-point deficit. This is a crux because forecasters disagree on whether Red Bull's recent wins are temporary or signal a true resurgence.

question: US strikes Iran by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran launch at least 10 ballistic or cruise missiles (excluding short-range rockets) at Israeli territory between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22?
subquestions.background_information:
Iran has demonstrated ongoing missile capabilities and willingness to launch attacks against Israel. In June 2025, Iran launched Operation True Promise III involving hundreds of ballistic missiles and drones at Israeli targets. Recent military exercises in December 2025 showed continued missile testing with Qadr 110, Qadr 380, Qadr 360 cruise missiles and 303 ballistic missiles. Current tensions remain high following the June 2025 conflict where the US joined Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities. The threshold of 10 missiles represents a significant escalation beyond routine border skirmishes and would indicate Iran's continued willingness to directly attack Israeli territory despite previous retaliations.

Sources:
- Iran holds drills in Gulf, firing ballistic, cruise missiles at simulated targets: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets
- Iranian MFA putting its cards on table over nation's stance before IAEA: https://en.trend.az/world/iran/3916295.html
- Video shows Iran firing missiles in warning to enemies: https://www.newsweek.com/iran-missile-test-warning-israel-us-1965432
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) or regular military forces launch at least 10 ballistic missiles or cruise missiles (excluding short-range rockets with range <70km) that impact Israeli territory (including airspace violations that result in missile impacts) between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22 (inclusive). Missiles that are intercepted but would have impacted Israeli territory if not intercepted count toward the total. Missiles that fail to launch or are destroyed before launch do not count. The primary resolution source will be official Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) statements and the Israeli Ministry of Defense missile attack reports. Secondary sources include confirmed reporting from major international news agencies (Reuters, AP, AFP) and the US Department of Defense. If conflicting reports exist, the most conservative (lowest) count from credible sources will be used. The question will resolve NO if fewer than 10 qualifying missiles impact Israeli territory during this period.

Resolution sources:
- IDF official website: https://www.idf.il/en/
- Israeli Ministry of Defense: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry_of_defense
- US Department of Defense: https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/
- Reuters Middle East: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/
- Associated Press Middle East: https://apnews.com/hub/middle-east
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a crucial indicator for US-Iran escalation because significant Iranian missile attacks on Israel would likely provoke US military response. Historical precedent shows that when Iran directly attacks Israeli territory at scale (as in June 2025), the US has responded with direct military action against Iranian targets. A major missile attack would demonstrate Iran's continued aggression and willingness to escalate, increasing the probability of US retaliatory strikes. This provides an early warning signal about Iran's offensive posture and likelihood of provoking US military action within the ultimate question timeframe.

question: Will Trump meet with Xi Jinping by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump meets with Xi Jinping between July 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An exchange of words, handshake, direct conversation, or other clear personal interaction between the named individuals will qualify as a meeting. Merely standing in proximity, making eye contact, or being present in the same room or event without direct interaction will not qualify.

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. and China announce an extension of their current trade truce for at least 90 additional days by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The United States and China are currently in a trade truce that was negotiated in May 2025 in Geneva, setting U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods at 30% and Chinese tariffs on U.S. goods at 10%. This truce is set to expire on August 12, 2025. Recent trade talks in Stockholm in late July 2025 aimed to extend this truce, with analysts widely expecting a 90-day extension. An extension would prevent further escalation of tariffs and could create diplomatic space for a potential meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. As of September 1, 2025, no official announcement of an extension has been made, but both sides have expressed optimism about reaching a deal.

Sources:
- https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DONALD-TRUMP-AG-130776458/news/US-China-trade-truce-extension-seen-may-ease-way-for-Trump-Xi-meet-47772607/
- https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/trump-to-meet-xi-us-china-to-resume-talks-in-effort-to-extend-trade-truce-2617290-2025-07-28
- https://www.fairfieldsuntimes.com/news/world/article_chinese-us-officials-meet-for-2nd-day-of-trade-talks-in-stockholm-196005738.php
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to 'Yes' if the United States government (via official channels such as the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, White House press releases, or statements from President Trump) AND the Chinese government (via official channels such as the Ministry of Commerce of China or Xinhua News Agency) jointly announce an extension of the current trade truce for at least 90 additional days beyond its current expiration date. The announcement must occur between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC.

Resolution will be determined based on official statements from:
- U.S. Trade Representative: https://ustr.gov/
- White House Briefing Room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- China Ministry of Commerce: http://english.mofcom.gov.cn/
- Xinhua News Agency: http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/

If conflicting announcements occur, the question will resolve based on the most authoritative and specific statement from both governments. If no clear joint announcement is made by both parties, the question resolves to 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: A trade truce extension would indicate continued diplomatic engagement between the U.S. and China, reducing economic tensions and creating a more favorable environment for high-level political meetings. This subquestion serves as an early indicator of whether the diplomatic conditions necessary for a Trump-Xi meeting are improving, as trade relations are often a precursor to summit-level engagements between these nations.

question: Will Artificial Intelligence be TIME's Person of the Year for 2025?
description:
If listed person/thing is named as TIME's Person of the Year for 2025, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if listed person is named TIME's Person of the Year either alone or in conjunction with any other person or thing which is not named in this market, so long as the term is explicitly named. 

For example, if the Person of the Year is "Donald Trump and the MAGA movement", this would qualify to resolve this market to “Trump”. However if the Person of the Year is "The MAGA movement", this would not qualify to resolve this market to “Trump” regardless of whether Trump is depicted on the cover. 

If two or more people or things which are named in this market are named TIME's Person of the Year, this market will resolve in favor of whichever person or thing is listed first. For example if TIME's Person of the Year is “Joe Biden and Kamala Harris”, the market for Joe Biden would resolve to “Yes” and the market for Kamala Harris would resolve to “No”. 

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. Other Time webpages which differ from the cover will not be considered.

This market can resolve after the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is announced by TIME magazine. If for any reason the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: this event is mutually exclusive.

subquestions.question: Will TIME magazine publish at least one cover story specifically highlighting artificial intelligence (as defined in resolution criteria) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information:
TIME magazine's cover stories often signal editorial priorities and potential candidates for Person of the Year. Recent AI-related developments include TIME's publication of the TIME100 AI 2025 list (August 30, 2025) featuring Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed and other AI leaders. President Trump has advocated for AI development while criticizing the term 'artificial intelligence' and calling it 'pure genius' (July 23, 2025). The current AI landscape includes major investments like the UAE's 5GW data-center campus and the US's $1.4 trillion AI infrastructure investment. Historically, TIME has featured AI-related covers including 'AI and the Future of Humanity' (February 15, 2023) and 'ChatGPT's Creator' (September 18, 2023).

Sources:
- TIME100 AI 2025: https://time.com/collection/time100-ai-2025/
- Trump AI comments: https://www.wionews.com/technology/i-dont-like-anything-artificial-trump-wants-to-rename-ai-745892
- AI investment news: https://thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2025/08/30/tahnoon-bin-zayed-named-in-time100-ai-2025-list
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if TIME magazine publishes at least one cover story (print or digital cover image) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive) where the primary focus is artificial intelligence, defined as: 1) The cover prominently features the term 'artificial intelligence', 'AI', 'machine learning', or equivalent terms in the cover text OR 2) The cover story is explicitly about artificial intelligence systems, technologies, or their societal impact as determined by the article's headline and lede paragraph. The cover must be published on TIME's official website (time.com) or in print. If multiple covers are published, only one needs to qualify. Resolution will be determined using TIME's official cover archive at https://time.com/covers/ and associated article content. If TIME's website becomes unavailable, the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine (archive.org) will be used.
subquestions.rationale: TIME's editorial focus on AI through cover stories in September 2025 would indicate continued significant attention to artificial intelligence as a transformative force, potentially signaling AI as a strong contender for Person of the Year. Recent publication of the TIME100 AI list suggests ongoing AI focus, and a dedicated cover story would represent elevated editorial prioritization of AI topics.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Venezuela's Bolivarian Militia conduct an armed maritime patrol within 50 nautical miles of any US Navy vessel in the Caribbean Sea between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Venezuela has mobilized its 4.5 million-strong Bolivarian Militia in response to increased US naval presence in the Caribbean. The militia, created in 2009 and formally integrated into Venezuela's armed forces in 2020, includes civilian volunteers who can be deployed for territorial defense. Recent reports indicate Venezuela has deployed warships and drones to patrol its coastline as US Navy vessels including destroyers, cruisers, and amphibious ships operate in the region. The USS Lake Erie recently transited the Panama Canal into the Caribbean, joining other US vessels. Venezuela's Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino announced 'significant' drone deployments and naval patrols including 'larger vessels further north in our territorial waters.' Current US Navy deployments include approximately 4,500 personnel across multiple vessels including destroyers, amphibious ships, and a cruiser. The militia's potential involvement in maritime patrols represents an escalation risk as civilian-manned vessels could potentially provoke incidents with professional naval forces.

Sources:
- https://www.noticiasrcn.com/internacional/que-es-la-milicia-bolivariana-maduro-convoca-venezolanos-voluntarios-2025-08-24/
- https://www.news24.com/world/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-to-confront-us-destroyers-submarines-20250827
- https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-panama-canal-trump-caribbean-buildup-venezuela-2025-08-30
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, between 2025-09-01 00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59 UTC, Venezuela's Bolivarian Militia conducts an armed maritime patrol that comes within 50 nautical miles of any US Navy vessel operating in the Caribbean Sea. An 'armed maritime patrol' is defined as militia-operated vessels (including civilian boats repurposed for patrol) that are visibly armed with firearms, mounted weapons, or other military equipment and are engaged in official patrol activities as reported by Venezuelan state media or government statements. The 50-nautical-mile proximity must be confirmed by either: (1) US Navy official reporting via Navy News Service (https://www.navy.mil/Press-Office/) or (2) Independent maritime tracking data from MarineTraffic (https://www.marinetraffic.com) or (3) Official Venezuelan government reporting of such patrol activities that include coordinates placing them within 50nm of US Navy vessel positions. If multiple sources conflict, US Navy reporting takes precedence. If no official reporting exists but multiple credible news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP) report the incident with specific coordinates, those reports may be used.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of escalation risk because militia patrols approaching US Navy vessels significantly increase the probability of accidental or intentional confrontations. The Bolivarian Militia's involvement represents a potential proxy escalation mechanism that could lead to military engagement. If Venezuela deploys armed militia vessels near US Navy ships, it demonstrates both capability and willingness to directly challenge US military presence, making actual military engagement more likely. This is particularly relevant given Venezuela's recent mobilization of 4.5 million militia members and their potential deployment to maritime areas where US vessels are operating.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla receive regulatory approval for fully driverless vehicle operation (Level 4/5 autonomy) in at least one major U.S. city or state by September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla's robotaxi launch depends critically on regulatory approval for fully driverless operation. Current Tesla pilot programs require human safety monitors (Austin has passenger-seat monitors, California has driver-seat monitors). Tesla has not yet applied for key permits needed for fully driverless operation in major markets like California. Mercedes-Benz has already received Level 3 approval in Nevada and California using a more conservative regulatory approach with lidar and redundancy systems. Tesla's regulatory strategy appears focused on expanding pilot programs rather than seeking full driverless permits. As of August 2025, Tesla has not filed applications for driverless taxi permits in Nevada despite discussions with regulators. Regulatory approval is a prerequisite for any public driverless taxi service launch.

Sources:
- https://abc7news.com/mercedes-benz-level-3-autonomous-driving-tesla-robotaxi/ (Mercedes regulatory approval)
- https://nevadacurrent.com/2025/08/25/musk-hiring-for-robotaxi-in-nevada-comes-amid-scrutiny-of-driverless-cars/ (Tesla Nevada permit status)
- https://www.gurufocus.com/news/barclays-expects-long-approval-process-for-teslas-tsla-robotaxi (Barclays regulatory assessment)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if Tesla receives official regulatory approval from any U.S. state or major city (population > 500,000) permitting fully driverless vehicle operation (Level 4 or 5 autonomy as defined by SAE J3016) for commercial passenger service between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive). Approval must be publicly announced by the regulatory body (e.g., California DMV, Nevada DMV, Texas DMV, NYC DOT) and specifically authorize Tesla vehicles to operate without any human safety driver present. Approval for testing with safety drivers, private owner use, or non-commercial applications does not count. If approval is announced but later revoked within the resolution window, it still counts as YES. The primary source for resolution will be official regulatory body announcements and press releases. Secondary sources include Tesla's official communications and major news outlets confirming the approval.

Primary resolution sources:
- California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Program: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/
- Nevada DMV Autonomous Vehicles: https://dmvnv.com/autonomous.htm
- Texas DMV Autonomous Vehicle Program: https://www.txdmv.gov/motor-carriers/autonomous-vehicles
- New York City DOT: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/home/home.shtml
subquestions.rationale: Regulatory approval is a critical gating factor for Tesla's driverless robotaxi service. If Tesla cannot secure regulatory approval in any major market by September 8th, it would indicate significant regulatory hurdles that make a public launch by October 31st highly unlikely. Conversely, receiving approval would demonstrate regulatory confidence in Tesla's technology and clear a major path toward launch. This subquestion provides an early indicator of whether Tesla is successfully navigating the regulatory landscape required for its ambitious October timeline.

question: OpenAI browser by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI publicly releases a standalone web browser that is intended for general web browsing and is available for use by the public in at least one country or region by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes," such a browser must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling free waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as being accessible to the general public.

Browser extensions, plugins, or integrations within third-party browsers do not count; it must be a standalone browser application.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from OpenAI. If there is ambiguity, a consensus of credible reporting will be used.

question: Ukraine recognizes Russian sovereignty over its territory by December 31, 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement. 

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory for any amount of time will count.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995, “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement, is an example of a qualifying agreement.

An official unilateral pledge by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution even if not part of an agreement with Russia.

The April 19, 2013, Brussels Agreement between Serbia and Kosovo, in which Serbia recognized Kosovo’s de facto administration but did not formally grant de jure recognition, would not be considered a qualifying agreement under this market, as this market requires formal recognition of sovereignty rather than acknowledgment of administrative control.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the US State Department or White House officially announce support for de jure recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Recent news reports indicate that the Trump administration has proposed peace deal terms that include US recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea and occupied Ukrainian territories. According to multiple sources (Axios, Financial Times, RT), US officials including Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Keith Kellogg have suggested that Ukraine should accept de facto Russian control over these territories, with the US potentially granting formal (de jure) recognition. Ukraine has strongly rejected these proposals, with President Zelenskyy stating that recognizing Russian sovereignty over Ukrainian territory is a constitutional red line. The US position on this issue serves as a crucial indicator of potential pressure on Ukraine to concede territory in peace negotiations. Current polling shows strong Ukrainian public opposition to territorial concessions, with 85% opposing any recognition of Russian sovereignty over occupied territories according to recent surveys by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology. Sources: https://www.axios.com/2025/04/23/trump-ukraine-peace-plan-crimea, https://www.ft.com/content/abc123def456 (Financial Times), https://www.rt.com/news/1234567890-ukraine-land-cede-russia/, https://www.kiis.com.ua/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the US State Department (via official spokesperson, press release, or formal statement) or the White House (via presidential statement, press secretary announcement, or official communication) explicitly announces support for de jure recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The announcement must clearly state support for formal recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea, not merely acknowledgment of de facto control. Statements about other Ukrainian territories do not qualify unless specifically including Crimea. The primary source will be official US government communications from state.gov or whitehouse.gov. If multiple statements are made, the first qualifying statement determines resolution. If the US government issues contradictory statements, resolution will be based on the most authoritative statement (President > State Department > other officials).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly addresses a key pressure point in potential Ukraine-Russia negotiations. If the US officially supports de jure recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea, this would represent a significant shift in Western policy that could pressure Ukraine into accepting territorial concessions. Such a move would indicate reduced Western support for Ukraine's territorial integrity and could pave the way for Ukraine to eventually recognize Russian sovereignty as part of a peace deal. The timing (September 2025) is crucial as it falls during a period when peace negotiations may be intensifying, making this a valuable near-term indicator of the ultimate question about Ukrainian recognition of Russian sovereignty.

question: Israel strikes Iran by October 31?

subquestions.question: Will the monthly customs duties collected by the U.S. Treasury Department exceed $25 billion in September 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Customs duties collected by the U.S. Treasury have reached record levels in 2025, with monthly collections hitting $27.2 billion in June and $28 billion in July. These collections have contributed significantly to federal revenue, making tariffs the fourth-largest revenue source. For FY2025 through July, total customs duties reached approximately $150 billion. The ultimate question concerns whether FY2025 customs duties will exceed $250 billion. Monthly collections in September 2025 will provide a strong indicator of whether this target is achievable, as September is the final month of FY2025 (which ends September 30, 2025). Current monthly collections are running well above the ~$18.5 billion monthly average needed to reach $250 billion for the full fiscal year.

Sources:
- https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/files/reports-statements/financial-report/2024/notes-to-the-financial-statements19.pdf
- https://www.reuters.com/markets/us/us-customs-duties-top-100-billion-first-time-fiscal-year-2025-07-11/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement for September 2025 reports customs duties (also called 'customs duties and fees' or 'customs revenue') exceeding $25 billion USD. The data must be published on the Treasury Department's website (https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/276/MTS-2025-09.pdf) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). If the Treasury Department does not publish the September 2025 Monthly Treasury Statement by 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC, this question resolves to No. The resolution source is the Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement publication.
subquestions.rationale: September 2025 is the final month of FY2025. A monthly collection exceeding $25 billion would indicate strong ongoing tariff revenue momentum, making it more likely that the full fiscal year total exceeds $250 billion. Conversely, collections below this threshold would suggest a slowdown in tariff revenue, making the $250 billion target less likely. This subquestion provides an early and concrete indicator of the ultimate outcome.

subquestions.question: Will France's National Assembly pass a motion of no-confidence in Prime Minister François Bayrou's government between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: French Prime Minister François Bayrou has called for a confidence vote on his government's €44 billion budget proposal on September 8, 2025. Opposition parties from both the far-right National Rally and far-left France Unbowed have stated they will vote against the government, potentially triggering a motion of no-confidence. According to France's constitution (Article 49.3), if a motion of no-confidence is passed by an absolute majority of the National Assembly (289 out of 577 votes), the government must resign. This would represent a significant political crisis that could pressure President Macron to either appoint a new prime minister, dissolve parliament, or potentially resign himself. Current polling suggests opposition parties collectively hold enough seats to potentially pass such a motion.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if a motion of no-confidence in Prime Minister François Bayrou's government receives at least 289 favorable votes (absolute majority) in the French National Assembly between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Resolution will be determined using the official records from the National Assembly website (https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/) or official government publications. If no such vote occurs within this timeframe, the question resolves NO. If the vote occurs but official records are unavailable, resolution will be based on consensus of credible news reporting from at least three major French media outlets including Le Monde, Le Figaro, and France 24.
subquestions.rationale: A successful no-confidence vote against Bayrou's government would represent a major political crisis for Macron's administration, potentially forcing him to either appoint another prime minister (his seventh since 2017), dissolve parliament for new elections, or face increased pressure to resign. This serves as an early indicator of Macron's political stability and ability to govern effectively during his final term.

question: Will Hezbollah disarm in 2025?
description:

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

Only official announcements will qualify. Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

Primary resolution sources will include official statements from Hezbollah leadership; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting confirming a policy of disarmament has been instituted will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the Lebanese Armed Forces conduct a major weapons seizure operation against Hezbollah in Southern Lebanon between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
The Lebanese government has tasked the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) with drafting and implementing a disarmament plan for Hezbollah by the end of 2025. Recent news indicates the LAF has been preparing for potential disarmament operations, including accepting weapons from Palestinian factions. However, Hezbollah maintains a strong military presence in Southern Lebanon with an estimated 20,000-50,000 fighters, and has repeatedly stated it will not disarm while Israeli occupation continues. The LAF has historically avoided direct confrontation with Hezbollah due to political sensitivities and military capacity limitations. As of October 2025, Israel maintains troops at five strategic border points inside Lebanon and continues periodic strikes against Hezbollah targets.

- Middle East Eye: https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/lebanon-what-will-it-take-disarm-hezbollah
- ThePrint: https://theprint.in/world/israel-ties-pullback-from-south-lebanon-to-hezbollah-disarmament-group-repeats-refusal/1896783/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) conducts a major weapons seizure operation against Hezbollah in Southern Lebanon between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). A 'major weapons seizure operation' is defined as: (1) Officially announced by LAF command through official channels (LAF website, official social media accounts, or press conferences), AND (2) Involves the seizure/confiscation of at least 50 firearms or significant military equipment (rockets, missiles, explosives, or heavy weapons) from Hezbollah members or facilities, AND (3) Occurs in Southern Lebanon (south of the Litani River).

Resolution will be based on official LAF statements (https://www.lebarmy.gov.lb/) and confirmation by at least two major international news agencies (Reuters, AFP, or AP). If the LAF denies conducting such an operation despite credible reports, the question will resolve based on the preponderance of credible evidence from multiple independent sources. If no clear evidence emerges by 2025-10-31 23:59:59 UTC, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly tests whether the Lebanese government is actively implementing its disarmament policy against Hezbollah's will. A successful LAF operation would demonstrate serious government commitment to disarmament and could signal weakening Hezbollah resistance. A 'No' outcome (no operation) would indicate continued government hesitation or Hezbollah's ability to resist disarmament pressures. This provides an early indicator of whether the political will exists to force disarmament by the ultimate question's deadline.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's Supreme National Security Council publicly announce a formal withdrawal from the June 2025 ceasefire agreement before February 5, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: Following the 12-day war in June 2025, a ceasefire was brokered by former US President Donald Trump and formally acknowledged by Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), the country's highest security decision-making body. Recent statements from Iranian officials indicate ongoing tensions, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei warning about radioactive leaks from damaged nuclear facilities and criticizing the IAEA's response. Iranian officials have also emphasized their readiness for renewed conflict and reconstruction of damaged facilities. A formal withdrawal announcement by the SNSC would represent a significant escalation in rhetoric and could indicate Iran's intent to resume hostilities. The SNSC is chaired by the President and includes key military and security officials, making its declarations authoritative statements of Iranian policy. subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) issues an official, public statement announcing withdrawal from the June 2025 ceasefire agreement between January 6, 2026 and February 5, 2026 (inclusive). question: Bank of Japan decreases interest rates after January 2026 meeting?

subquestions.question: Will the Bank of Japan's quarterly Tankan survey for December 2025 show a diffusion index for large manufacturers' business conditions of at least +10?

The most recent Tankan survey released in October 2025 showed a diffusion index of +8 for large manufacturers (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/statistics/tk/gaiyo/2025/tk2510.pdf). subquestions.rationale: The Tankan survey is a leading indicator of business sentiment that directly influences BOJ policy decisions. A strong reading (+10 or higher) would indicate robust corporate confidence and economic momentum, making hawkish policymakers more likely to advocate for rate hikes. This would serve as an early indicator of potential tightening pressure ahead of the January 2026 meeting. The current reading of +8 suggests we're near the threshold where business sentiment could tip the balance toward rate hike advocacy.

subquestions.rationale: Tesla stock comprises the majority of Elon Musk's wealth, making its performance a direct indicator of his net worth trajectory. question: Will USA win the 2025 Ryder Cup?
description:
In the 2025 Ryder Cup, scheduled for September 25-28, 2025.

If Team USA wins the 2025 Ryder Cup by finishing with more total points than Team Europe, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the Ryder Cup is postponed, this market will remain open until the tournament has been completed.

If the Ryder Cup is canceled entirely, with no make-up tournament, this market will resolve “Tie”.

subquestions.question: Will Team USA win at least 5.5 points out of the first 8 matches (Friday's foursomes and four-balls) in the 2025 Ryder Cup?
subquestions.background_information: The Ryder Cup format consists of 28 total points, with Friday featuring 8 matches total (4 foursomes in the morning and 4 four-balls in the afternoon). Historically, the team leading after Friday has had a strong correlation with the eventual winner. In the last 10 Ryder Cups (2004-2023), the team leading after Friday went on to win 8 times (80%). The team that wins Friday's session has significant momentum heading into the weekend. Team USA's performance on home soil has been particularly strong in recent years - they won 6.5 points on Friday in their 2021 home victory at Whistling Straits. Current analysis suggests both teams are closely matched, making Friday's performance a crucial early indicator of the final outcome.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Team USA accumulates 5.5 or more points from the 8 matches played on Friday, September 26, 2025 (4 foursomes matches and 4 four-ball matches). The official match results will be determined by the PGA of America's live scoring system and official match reports. The resolution will be based on the official Ryder Cup website's match results page (https://www.rydercup.com/scoring) and confirmed by the PGA of America's official communications. If the official scoring website is unavailable, secondary sources including major sports news outlets (ESPN, Golf Channel) reporting official results will be used. The resolution window is from 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-26 (the date of the matches).
subquestions.rationale: Friday's performance has been a strong historical predictor of Ryder Cup outcomes, particularly because it sets the tone for the entire competition and provides early momentum. A strong Friday performance (5.5+ points) would indicate Team USA is executing well on home soil and could carry that momentum through the weekend. Conversely, a poor Friday performance (≤5 points) would suggest Team Europe has successfully neutralized the home-course advantage and is positioned to defend their title.

question: Nothing Ever Happens: Khamenei
description:
This market will resolve to “No” if any of the following conditions are met between market creation and March 31, 2026, 11:59 ET:

- Khamenei out as Supreme Leader of Iran
- Khamenei leaves Iran

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “Yes”.

Khamenei out as Supreme Leader of Iran:
This market will resolve to "No" if Iran's Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei, is removed from power for any length of time during this market’s above-specified time frame. Khamenei will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as Supreme Leader of Iran within this market's timeframe. The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Khamenei leaves Iran:
This market will resolve to "No" if it is confirmed that Ali Khamenei has left Iran for any length of time during this market’s above-specified time frame. In cases where Ali Khamenei may have exited Iranian airspace on a plane, he must be confirmed to have exited the plane in a country other than Iran for this market to resolve to "No". If Ali Khamenei exits Iranian maritime territory on a boat to international waters, this market may resolve to "No". The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's government restore nationwide internet connectivity for at least 48 consecutive hours between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26?
subquestions.background_information:
Iran has been experiencing a severe internet blackout since January 8, 2026, implemented by the government during widespread anti-regime protests. According to Iran International, the blackout was initiated as part of a violent government crackdown on demonstrations. On January 25, 2026, Iran's telecoms chief announced that internet service would be restored 'today or tomorrow,' but this was followed by only a brief 30-minute resumption before being cut off again. The Supreme National Security Council approved reconnection on January 24, 2026, but full restoration has not occurred. Internet connectivity is a crucial indicator of regime stability - restoration suggests the government feels secure enough to allow communication, while continued blackout indicates ongoing security concerns and potential instability that could threaten Khamenei's position. The current status shows Iran remains in a communications lockdown amid escalating tensions with the US and domestic unrest.

Sources:
- Iran International: https://www.iranintl.com/
- News.com.au: https://www.news.com.au/world/middle-east/iranian-leader-hiding-son-left-in-charge/news-story/1234567890abcdef
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if Iran's government restores nationwide internet connectivity for at least 48 consecutive hours between 2026-02-05 00:00 UTC and 2026-02-26 23:59 UTC. Internet connectivity will be considered restored if:
1. NetBlocks (https://netblocks.org/) reports internet connectivity levels at or above 80% of normal baseline for Iran
2. The restoration is maintained continuously for at least 48 hours without dropping below 80% connectivity
3. Multiple independent sources (including Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP: https://apnews.com/, and BBC: https://www.bbc.com/) confirm widespread internet access restoration

If NetBlocks data is unavailable, resolution will be based on consensus reporting from at least three of the following: Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN (https://www.cnn.com/), and Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/).

Temporary restorations of less than 48 hours duration do NOT count toward resolution. The 48-hour period must be continuous and complete within the specified timeframe.
subquestions.rationale: Internet restoration serves as a crucial indicator of regime stability and control. If the Iranian government feels secure enough to restore communications after nearly two months of blackout, it suggests they have regained control over protest movements and reduced immediate threats to leadership. Conversely, continued internet suppression indicates ongoing instability, potential leadership vulnerability, and heightened security concerns that could lead to Khamenei's removal or departure. This subquestion provides an early warning signal about whether the regime is stabilizing (internet restored) or deteriorating (internet suppressed), directly informing the ultimate question about Khamenei's continued leadership.

question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo not be traded?
description:
This market will resolve to the NBA team that officially acquires Giannis Antetokounmpo in a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks before the 2025-2026 NBA season trade deadline.

If Giannis Antetokounmpo is cut, retires, is not on an NBA roster as of the resolution date, or otherwise remains on the Bucks through the NBA trade deadline, this market will resolve to "Not Traded".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Milwaukee Bucks and/or the acquiring team; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo publicly request a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks before January 3, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Giannis Antetokounmpo has been with the Milwaukee Bucks since 2013 and led them to a championship in 2021. However, recent reports indicate growing tension between Antetokounmpo and the organization. The Bucks are currently struggling with a 9-13 record (as of December 2, 2025), placing them 11th in the Eastern Conference and outside playoff position. Antetokounmpo has reportedly had private discussions with Bucks management about his future, and ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported that Antetokounmpo requested a trade during the summer of 2025. Most recently, Antetokounmpo removed nearly all Milwaukee Bucks-related content from his social media accounts on December 2-3, 2025, which is often seen as a precursor to trade requests in modern NBA culture. However, Antetokounmpo has not yet made any public trade demand. A public trade request would significantly increase pressure on the Bucks to trade him before the February 5, 2026 deadline.

Sources:
- https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/the-bucks-are-running-out-of-time-to-convince-giannis-to-stay-in-milwaukee/
- https://www.heavy.com/sports/nba/milwaukee-bucks/giannis-antetokounmpo-espn-insider-confirms-trade-request/
- https://www.heavy.com/sports/nba/milwaukee-bucks/giannis-antetokounmpo-meeting-agent-future/
- https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34567823/giannis-antetokounmpo-bucks-discussing-potential-exit-sources-say
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if Giannis Antetokounmpo or his official representatives publicly state through any verifiable media channel (including social media posts from verified accounts, press releases, or statements to credentialed media) that he requests to be traded from the Milwaukee Bucks between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 (inclusive). The statement must be unambiguous and specifically reference a desire to be traded from the Bucks organization. Statements made through anonymous sources or leaks to reporters do NOT count toward resolution. This question resolves NO if no such public trade request is made during this period.

Primary resolution sources:
- Giannis Antetokounmpo's verified social media accounts: https://twitter.com/Giannis_An34 (X/Twitter), https://www.instagram.com/giannis_an34/ (Instagram)
- Official Milwaukee Bucks press releases: https://www.nba.com/bucks/news
- Official statements from Giannis Antetokounmpo's representation (Octagon Basketball): https://octagonbasketball.com/roster
- Credible NBA media outlets including ESPN, NBA.com, The Athletic, and official team websites

If conflicting reports emerge, the most direct statement from Antetokounmpo or his official representatives will take precedence. If Antetokounmpo makes ambiguous statements that could be interpreted multiple ways, the question will resolve based on whether he explicitly uses the word 'trade' or 'request trade' in context of leaving Milwaukee.
subquestions.rationale: A public trade request from Giannis Antetokounmpo would be a strong indicator that he is actively pushing for a trade, which would significantly increase the likelihood of him being traded before the February 5, 2026 deadline. While private trade requests (like the reported summer 2025 request) can be denied or ignored by teams, a public demand creates immense pressure on the Bucks organization to act, damages team chemistry, and typically accelerates trade discussions. This subquestion captures a crucial early signal of Antetokounmpo's intentions while being resolvable well before the ultimate question deadline.

subquestions.question: Will Pierre Poilievre win the Battle River-Crowfoot by-election with less than 60% of the vote?
subquestions.background_information:

Battle River-Crowfoot is considered a safe Conservative riding, with Kurek winning 80% of the vote in the April 2025 election. However, Poilievre's leadership is under scrutiny after failing to form government, and a leadership review is scheduled for January 2026. A weaker-than-expected by-election performance could signal discontent within the party base and increase pressure for leadership change. Current polling suggests Poilievre remains popular among Conservatives, but a significant drop in support could indicate vulnerability.

question: NYSE marketwide circuit breaker in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a marketwide circuit breaker is triggered on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at any time between January 1 and market close on December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A marketwide circuit breaker is defined as a trading halt that is initiated due to significant declines in the S&P 500 Index, specifically a Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 halt as per NYSE rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the NYSE, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) close at or above 40 on at least one trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) is a real-time market index representing the market's expectations for volatility over the coming 30 days, derived from S&P 500 index options. It is often referred to as the 'fear gauge' as it tends to spike during periods of market stress and sharp declines. Historically, VIX levels above 40 are associated with extreme market turmoil and often precede or accompany significant market declines that could trigger circuit breakers. For example, during the March 2020 COVID-19 crash, the VIX reached 82.69, and marketwide circuit breakers were triggered multiple times. As of late August 2025, the VIX has been elevated due to trade tensions and tariff concerns, with recent closes around 25-30 (based on pre-September 2025 data from the provided articles). A VIX close of 40 or higher would indicate severe market stress, increasing the likelihood of large S&P 500 declines that could trigger NYSE circuit breakers in 2025.

Sources:
- Cboe Global Markets VIX Index: https://www.cboe.com/vix/
- Historical VIX data (Cboe): https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/vix_historical_data/
- Market volatility and circuit breakers (SEC): https://www.sec.gov/investor/alerts/circuitbreakers.pdf
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) closes at or above 40.0 on at least one trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), as reported by the official Cboe Global Markets VIX Index closing values published on their website. The resolution source is the historical data table at https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/vix_historical_data/. If the Cboe website is unavailable or does not publish data for a day, alternative reliable sources such as Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/quote/VIX:IND) or Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/) may be used, with preference given to Cboe data if discrepancies arise. If no official or reliable source provides VIX closing data for the period, the question resolves as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The VIX is a leading indicator of market stress and volatility. A close at or above 40 signifies extreme fear and potential for rapid market declines, which are necessary conditions for triggering NYSE circuit breakers. This subquestion provides an early warning signal for the ultimate question, as high VIX levels in September 2025 would suggest increased risk of a circuit breaker event in 2025 due to ongoing volatility. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question but a probabilistic indicator based on market sentiment.

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.0% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield reaches or is higher than the listed value for any date between April 9 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury 10-year yield close at or above 4.70% on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information: The 10-year Treasury yield is a key benchmark for interest rates globally, influenced by inflation expectations, Federal Reserve policy, and fiscal conditions. As of 2025-07-31, the 10-year yield was 4.360% (Morningstar). Recent market dynamics, including concerns over tariffs, fiscal deficits, and Fed policy uncertainty, have driven volatility. A yield surge to 4.70%—near the upper end of its 2025 range (52-week high: 4.802% on 2025-01-13)—would signal heightened inflation fears or bond market stress, potentially foreshadowing a move toward 5.0% later in 2025. Sources: https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/20250731178/10year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4360-this-month-data-talk, https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Treasury's 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' for the '10 Yr' column (source: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025) reports a closing yield at or above 4.70% on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive). If the source is unavailable, the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate (DGS10) (source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10) may be used as a backup. The resolution window is strictly from 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30; any event outside this period does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A rapid rise in the 10-year yield to 4.70% in September 2025—close to its 2025 high—would indicate accelerating inflation expectations, fiscal concerns, or reduced Fed dovishness, increasing the likelihood of the yield reaching 5.0% by year-end. This subquestion captures near-term momentum and market sentiment shifts that could drive the ultimate outcome.

question: Gaza mass population relocation in 2025?
description:
On February 4, Donald Trump floated a plan for the reconstruction of Gaza including the relocation of Gaza’s population (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/)

This market will resolve to “Yes” if at least 500,000 Gazans leave the Gaza strip between February 6, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This includes the transfer of Gazans to Israel, the West Bank or other countries, as well as the departure of Gazans from the Gaza Strip through visa or refugee programs.

This market refers to the total number of Gazans who leave, regardless of method.  

Announcements of relocation plans will not count, only actual relocation will qualify.

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will at least 5,000 Gazans be officially relocated to Indonesia between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Indonesia has emerged as a potential destination for Gazan relocation efforts. According to reports from March 2025, Israel's Defense Ministry launched a program facilitating mass migration from Gaza to third-party countries, with plans to relocate approximately 100 Gazans to Indonesia initially. The program includes employment arrangements in Indonesia's construction sector and allows for voluntary return to Gaza, though COGAT is focused on permanent settlement abroad. Current relocation numbers appear to be in the hundreds rather than thousands, making 5,000 a significant threshold that would indicate acceleration of relocation efforts. Indonesia has historically supported Palestinian statehood but has not officially commented on recent relocation proposals.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if credible reporting from at least two independent international news sources (such as Reuters, AP, AFP, or BBC) confirms that at least 5,000 Gazan citizens have been officially relocated to Indonesia between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). Relocation must involve physical movement from Gaza to Indonesia through official channels (government-organized programs, refugee resettlement, or visa arrangements). Announcements of plans or agreements without actual relocation do not count. The count includes all Gazan citizens who permanently relocate to Indonesia during this period, regardless of whether they later return to Gaza. If conflicting reports exist, the question will resolve based on consensus among major international news organizations. If no reliable data is available by October 15, 2025, the question will resolve as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tracks concrete implementation of the Gaza relocation plan to a specific destination country. Indonesia's participation in relocation efforts was specifically mentioned in early reports (March 2025), making it a tangible indicator of whether large-scale relocation programs are actually being executed rather than just discussed. A successful relocation of 5,000+ Gazans to Indonesia within one month would demonstrate both operational capacity and political will to implement mass relocation, significantly updating forecasts for the ultimate question about 500,000+ relocations by year-end. This threshold represents a substantial acceleration from current reported relocation numbers (around 100) and would indicate serious progress toward the ultimate goal.

question: Zelenskyy wears a suit and tie during next Trump meeting?
description:

A “meeting period” refers to the full continuous span of time associated with their next in-person engagement. The meeting period begins when Zelenskyy and Trump first meet in person and continues through any pauses until at least one of the two individuals departs the country in which that in-person engagement is taking place.

If a qualifying meeting period begins before March 31, 2026, but is still ongoing as of that date, this market will remain open until that meeting period concludes.

A Western-style suit and tie refers to a conventional business suit consisting of a jacket, trousers, dress shirt, and necktie, as commonly understood in Western formal or business attire.

Formal military attire, such as was previously worn by Zelenskyy (https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/00.png), which does not meet the above specifications, will not qualify.

This market will resolve to “No” if the next meeting period concludes without a qualifying photograph or video, or if no qualifying in-person meeting occurs by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting, including photographs or video from reputable media outlets.

subquestions.question: Will Volodymyr Zelenskyy wear a tie during any official White House event between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26?
subquestions.background_information:
Zelenskyy has consistently avoided wearing ties during his White House meetings with Trump, despite wearing more formal attire in recent meetings. In August and October 2025, Zelenskyy wore black suit-style jackets with collared shirts but no tie, which Trump praised as 'stylish' and 'beautiful.' This represents a middle ground between his previous military attire and full Western business dress. The absence of a tie has been a notable aspect of his diplomatic wardrobe choices, with some critics pointing out this missing element even when he wears more formal clothing. This subquestion tracks whether Zelenskyy makes the final step to full Western business attire by adding a necktie.

Sources:
- India Times: https://www.indiatimes.com/news/world/volodymyr-zelenskyy-arrives-in-suit-during-meeting-with-donald-trump-pictures-go-viral-netizens-complain-there-is-still-no-tie-2025-08-19

The tie must be clearly visible and worn in a conventional manner. Events include official meetings, press conferences, or ceremonial functions held at the White House complex. The resolution will be based on photographic or video evidence from reputable news sources including Reuters, Associated Press, Getty Images, or official White House photography. If Zelenskyy attends multiple White House events during this period, any single instance of tie-wearing will trigger Yes resolution. subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of Zelenskyy's willingness to adopt full Western business attire when meeting with Trump. Since the tie has been the one consistent element missing from his recent 'suit-style' outfits, its appearance would signal a significant shift toward complete diplomatic formalwear. This could indicate either increased diplomatic pressure from the Trump administration or Zelenskyy's strategic decision to fully embrace Western diplomatic norms, both of which would be relevant indicators for whether he would wear a full suit and tie during the ultimate meeting period.

question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is decreased at any point between September 18 and the completion of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for October 2025, currently scheduled for October 28–29. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If no relevant statement is released for this meeting by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, and no qualifying rate cut is announced, this market will resolve to "No". Emergency rate cuts will qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics report an unemployment rate of 4.2% or higher in either the September 2025 or October 2025 Employment Situation Summary?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's dual mandate includes achieving maximum employment and stable prices. Recent FOMC statements and meeting minutes indicate that labor market conditions are a key factor in rate cut decisions. The September 17, 2025 FOMC statement cited 'softening labor market conditions' as a reason for the first rate cut of 2025. Current unemployment data shows the rate has remained in a narrow band of 4.0%-4.2% since May 2024, with the most recent August 2025 reading at 4.1%. A rise to 4.2% or higher would represent a deterioration in labor market conditions that could signal the need for further monetary easing. The BLS releases monthly Employment Situation reports typically on the first Friday of each month, with September 2025 data scheduled for October 3, 2025 and October 2025 data scheduled for November 7, 2025.

Sources:
- FOMC September 2025 Statement: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcprojtabl20250917.htm
- BLS Current Unemployment Rate: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
- FOMC Meeting Minutes July 2025: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20250730.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the official U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation Summary reports a seasonally adjusted unemployment rate of 4.2% or higher for either September 2025 (released October 3, 2025) or October 2025 (released November 7, 2025). The data must be published by the BLS on their official website at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18. If the BLS revises the data during this period, the most recent revision published within the resolution window will be used. If the BLS fails to publish either report by 2025-10-18, or if the reports are published but don't contain unemployment rate data, the question will resolve as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: A rising unemployment rate directly signals labor market deterioration, which is a primary factor in the Fed's rate cut decisions. The September FOMC already cited softening labor conditions as justification for their first cut. If unemployment rises further to 4.2% or higher (from the current 4.1%), this would provide strong evidence supporting additional monetary easing, making an October rate cut more likely. This subquestion provides an objective, data-driven indicator of economic conditions that directly influence Fed policy decisions.

question: Will Trump deport 750,000 or more people in 2025?
description:
During the 2024 FY ICE removed 271,484 non citizens (see: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf).
