subquestions.question: Will there be at least one magnitude 6.5 or higher earthquake in the Kamchatka Peninsula region (Russia) between November 13, 2025 and December 9, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia has experienced heightened seismic activity following a record-setting magnitude 8.8 earthquake on July 29, 2025, which was tied for the sixth-largest earthquake ever recorded. This event triggered thousands of aftershocks, including a magnitude 7.8 earthquake on September 19, 2025. According to the USGS, there is a 24% chance of another magnitude 7 or higher earthquake in the region in the months ahead, with a greater than 99% probability of continued magnitude 4.0+, 5.0+, and even M6.0+ events over the first year. The region's increased seismic activity makes it a potential indicator for global seismic patterns. As of November 2025, the region has experienced multiple moderate earthquakes including magnitude 5.2, 5.3, and 5.6 events in October 2025.

Sources:
- Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/two-earthquakes-rattle-russia-what-know-1976543
- Earthquake News Today: https://earthquakenewstoday.com/moderate-earthquake-5-6-mag-was-detected-near-vilyuchinsk-in-russia/
- USGS: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if at least one earthquake of magnitude 6.5 or higher occurs within the geographic region defined by latitude 50°N to 60°N and longitude 155°E to 165°E (Kamchatka Peninsula region) between November 13, 2025 00:00 UTC and December 9, 2025 23:59 UTC (inclusive). The magnitude threshold of 6.5 is selected as it represents a significant seismic event that would indicate continued major activity in this seismically active region.

Resolution will be determined using the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Catalog (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/). The USGS magnitude value (preferably the preferred magnitude type as listed in their catalog) will be used for resolution. If multiple magnitude values are reported, the highest authoritative magnitude will be used.

If the USGS data becomes unavailable or experiences significant delays, the question will resolve based on the next most authoritative international seismic monitoring source such as the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (https://www.emsc-csem.org/).

Edge case: If an earthquake occurs exactly on the boundary of the defined region, it will be considered within the region if its epicenter coordinates fall within the specified latitude and longitude ranges.
subquestions.rationale: The Kamchatka Peninsula region has been experiencing exceptionally high seismic activity following the July 2025 magnitude 8.8 earthquake, with USGS forecasting a 24% chance of another magnitude 7+ event in the coming months. A magnitude 6.5+ earthquake in this region within the next month would indicate that the significant aftershock sequence continues and increases the likelihood of major global seismic events. This subquestion provides an early indicator of whether the heightened seismic activity in one of the world's most active seismic zones is continuing, which could correlate with increased probability of magnitude 7.0+ earthquakes worldwide in the subsequent period.

subquestions.question: Will the CDC report at least 20 new confirmed measles cases in the U.S. between December 2, 2025 and December 31, 2025?

This represents a significant surge from previous years, with 2025 already surpassing the previous record of 1,274 cases in 2019. Current outbreaks are concentrated in Utah, Arizona, South Carolina, and New York, with 92% of cases occurring in unvaccinated individuals. The CDC reports that national vaccination coverage has declined to 92.5%, below the 95% threshold needed for herd immunity. The current weekly case rate (as of November 2025) suggests ongoing transmission that could continue through December 2025. Given that measles has an incubation period of 7-14 days and is highly contagious (each case can cause 12-18 new infections in unvaccinated populations), December case counts will serve as a strong indicator of whether transmission is continuing at levels that could lead to 500+ cases in 2026.

Sources:
- CDC Measles Data & Research: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the CDC's weekly measles surveillance report shows at least 20 new confirmed measles cases reported for the United States between December 2, 2025 (start date) and December 31, 2025 (end date), inclusive. If this source becomes unavailable, resolution will use archived versions from the Wayback Machine (archive.org) or official CDC press releases. If no weekly reports are published during this period, resolution will be based on the next available CDC report covering this timeframe. Cases must be confirmed measles (rubeola) cases in humans within the United States as defined by CDC criteria.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator for the ultimate question because ongoing measles transmission in December 2025 would strongly suggest that the conditions driving the current outbreak (low vaccination rates, susceptible populations, and efficient transmission) will persist into 2026. Given measles' high reproductive number and the timing of school terms/holiday gatherings in December, sustained transmission during this period would indicate that the U.S. is unlikely to achieve containment before 2026 begins. A 'Yes' outcome (≥20 cases) would suggest continued spread into 2026, making 500+ cases more likely, while a 'No' outcome would indicate successful containment efforts or seasonal decline in transmission.

question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?
description:

Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics cancels the release or is otherwise rendered incapable of releasing it by that time, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass a clean continuing resolution (CR) to fund the government by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The current government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, after Congress failed to pass appropriations bills. A continuing resolution (CR) is a temporary funding measure that would end the shutdown and allow agencies like the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) to resume normal operations, including data releases. The September jobs report was not released on October 4 due to the shutdown, and its future release depends on funding restoration. The House of Representatives must pass any funding legislation before it goes to the Senate and President. A 'clean CR' refers to a short-term funding bill without controversial policy riders that could complicate passage. Historical precedent shows that CRs are common solutions to end shutdowns (e.g., the 2013 and 2018-2019 shutdowns). This question tracks legislative progress toward resolving the shutdown, which is necessary for the BLS to release the jobs report. Sources: https://www.congress.gov/ (for bill status), https://www.cbo.gov/publication/59748 (CBO report on shutdown impacts), https://www.bls.gov/bls/update2025.htm (BLS contingency plan).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes a clean continuing resolution (CR) to fund the government between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). A 'clean CR' is defined as a bill that provides temporary funding for all or part of the federal government without substantive policy riders unrelated to appropriations. The passage must be confirmed by a roll-call vote recorded on the House Clerk's website (https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/) or via an official House press release (https://www.house.gov/). If multiple CRs are passed, the first one meeting these criteria resolves the question. If the CR includes minor provisions (e.g., technical corrections) but is primarily focused on funding, it still qualifies. If the CR is vetoed or fails in the Senate, the question still resolves Yes based on House passage. If no vote occurs or the CR fails in the House, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on whether the BLS can release the jobs report before the shutdown ends. A House-passed CR is a key legislative milestone indicating progress toward ending the shutdown. If the House passes a clean CR, it suggests a higher likelihood of the shutdown ending soon, enabling the BLS to release the report. Conversely, if the House fails to pass a CR by October 31, it indicates prolonged shutdown gridlock, making the BLS release less likely. This subquestion provides an early indicator of political momentum for resolution, which is directly linked to the ultimate outcome.

question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the US Bureau of Labor Statistics' November 2025 Employment Situation Report show an unemployment rate of 4.5% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions are heavily influenced by labor market conditions, particularly the unemployment rate. The ultimate question concerns whether the Fed will maintain a pause-pause-pause pattern in its December, January, and March meetings. Recent labor market data shows deterioration: the unemployment rate reached 4.3% in August 2025, the highest since October 2021, and job growth has significantly slowed. Fed officials including Michelle Bowman and Jerome Powell have expressed concerns about labor market weakness. A further deterioration in November's unemployment data (reaching 4.5% or higher) would significantly increase pressure on the Fed to continue rate cuts rather than pause, as it would indicate worsening employment conditions that conflict with the Fed's maximum employment mandate. The current unemployment rate is 4.3% (August 2025), and the Fed's dual mandate includes maintaining maximum employment alongside price stability.

Sources:
- Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com
- Goodreturns: https://www.goodreturns.in
- Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the US Bureau of Labor Statistics' Employment Situation Report for November 2025, which is scheduled for release on December 5, 2025, shows a seasonally adjusted unemployment rate of 4.5% or higher. The report must be published between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05 (inclusive). If the report is delayed beyond December 5, 2025, this question will resolve as No. The official source for resolution is the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Employment Situation Report at: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm. The unemployment rate is defined as the seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate as published in Table A-1 of the report.
subquestions.rationale: This question is highly relevant to the ultimate Fed pause-pause-pause question because labor market conditions are a primary driver of Fed policy decisions. A significant deterioration in the unemployment rate (reaching 4.5% or higher) would create strong pressure for the Fed to continue cutting rates rather than pausing, as it would indicate the labor market is weakening beyond acceptable levels for the Fed's maximum employment mandate. Conversely, if unemployment remains below 4.5%, it would give the Fed more flexibility to maintain rates or pause, supporting the pause-pause-pause scenario. This provides an early indicator of economic conditions that will heavily influence the December FOMC decision and subsequent meetings.

subquestions.question: Will the Consumer Confidence Index (CCI) from The Conference Board fall below 95.0 for September 2025?

The most recent available data shows the August 2025 CCI at 100.2 (seasonally adjusted), which represents a decline from previous months but remains above the 95.0 threshold. A reading below 95.0 would indicate significant consumer pessimism about current and future economic conditions, potentially signaling weaker consumer spending ahead. Historical data shows that when the CCI falls below 95.0, it often precedes economic slowdowns as consumers reduce spending.

- August 2025 CCI release: https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence/index

If The Conference Board changes its publication methodology or discontinues the index, resolution will be based on the most comparable successor index from the same organization.
subquestions.rationale: Consumer confidence is a strong leading indicator for GDP growth, as consumer spending accounts for the majority of US economic activity. Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar Games' parent company, holds quarterly earnings calls where they discuss financial performance and provide updates on upcoming releases. The next scheduled earnings call is expected in early November 2025 (historically around November 4-7). These calls are closely watched for any signals about GTA VI's development status. Current reporting indicates Take-Two has officially confirmed the May 26, 2026 release date in their September 2025 shareholder meeting, but industry insiders like Tom Henderson have suggested a potential delay announcement could come during the November earnings call. The November call represents the next major opportunity for Take-Two to communicate any changes to the planned release timeline.

Sources:
- https://ir.take2games.com/events-and-presentations (Take-Two Investor Relations)
- https://www.gameranx.com/updates/id/517220/article/insider-believes-a-grand-theft-auto-vi-delay-announcement-will-come-this-november/ (Gameranx article)
- https://www.sportskeeda.com/esports/gta-6-release-date-delay-rumors-everything-take-two-revealed-far (Sportskeeda article)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if during Take-Two Interactive's November 2025 earnings call (held between 2025-11-01 and 2025-11-07 inclusive), company executives explicitly mention any of the following regarding GTA VI: 1) potential delay beyond May 26, 2026, 2) development challenges impacting timeline, 3) timeline adjustments being considered, or 4) any statement indicating the May 26 date may not be met. The resolution will be based on the official earnings call transcript published by Take-Two Interactive at https://ir.take2games.com/events-and-presentations. General statements about 'quality focus' or 'polishing' without specific timeline implications do not count. If the earnings call does not occur within the specified window or no transcript is published, the question resolves as No.
subquestions.rationale: The November earnings call represents the next major corporate communication opportunity where Take-Two could signal potential delays. If executives mention timeline concerns or adjustments during this call, it would be a strong early indicator that the May 2026 release date is at risk, making a postponement more likely. Conversely, if they maintain strong confidence in the current timeline without any delay mentions, it suggests the project remains on track.

question: Will US GDP growth in 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted real GDP growth rate for the United States in 2025, as reported in the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) "Advance Estimate" release for Q4 of 2025, scheduled for January 29, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: The relevant data will be the full-year real GDP growth rate as stated in the advance estimate, typically expressed as the percentage change from the annual level in 2024 to the annual level in 2025. Any revisions to this figure made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the January 2026 US Consumer Confidence Index (Conference Board) reading be at least 110.0?
subquestions.background_information: Consumer confidence is a leading indicator of economic activity, as confident consumers are more likely to increase spending, which drives GDP growth. The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index is a widely watched monthly indicator. The most recent available data shows the November 2025 index at 105.7 (December 2025 data not yet released). Historically, consumer confidence above 100 indicates optimism, while levels below 80 often signal economic contraction risk. The January 2026 reading, typically released in late January, will provide insight into consumer sentiment at the beginning of 2026, which could influence spending patterns throughout the year.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for January 2026 is 110.0 or higher. The official reading will be obtained from the Conference Board's press release typically published on the last Tuesday of January (expected January 27, 2026). If the January 2026 reading is exactly 110.0, the question resolves Yes. If the Conference Board fails to release the January 2026 data by January 29, 2026, or if the data source becomes unavailable, the question will resolve based on the most authoritative alternative source available (e.g., University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index if it provides January 2026 data).
subquestions.rationale: Consumer confidence is a strong leading indicator for GDP growth, as consumer spending accounts for approximately 70% of US GDP. A reading of 110+ in January 2026 would suggest robust consumer optimism heading into 2026, increasing the likelihood of strong consumption-driven GDP growth throughout the year. This provides an early signal about economic momentum before the Q4 2025 GDP advance estimate is released.

question: Will Tulsi Gabbard be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve based on the next individual announced to leave the Trump Cabinet, or who otherwise ceases to be a member of the administration. If no one leaves by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”.

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Kristi Noem be removed or resign as Homeland Security Secretary by January 31, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
According to a December 7, 2025 report from The Bulwark, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem is expected to be removed from her position 'really soon' due to White House frustration with her continued employment of controversial adviser Corey Lewandowski. The report cites conversations with three former DHS officials who believe Trump may replace Noem imminently, potentially for a 'clean slate' at the start of 2026 to improve execution of mass deportation policies. However, Trump's decisions are described as fickle, and Noem might be retained through January-February 2026 to oversee planned enforcement operations. Noem was also mentioned in a December 15, 2025 Washington Post analysis as being on 'thin ice' and expected to be replaced in 2026. As of January 5, 2026, Noem remains in her position despite these reports.

Sources:
- The Bulwark: https://www.thebulwark.com/p/kristi-noem-expected-out-homeland-security
- Washington Post: https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2025/12/15/trump-cabinet-turnover-analysis/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Kristi Noem is officially removed from her position as Secretary of Homeland Security or submits a formal resignation that is accepted by President Trump between January 5, 2026 and January 31, 2026 (inclusive). Removal or resignation must be confirmed by either: 1) An official White House announcement via press release or presidential tweet, 2) DHS official communications confirming the departure, or 3) Major news outlets (AP, Reuters, CNN, Fox News, NYT, WaPo) reporting confirmation from White House or DHS officials. Acting appointments do not count - the position must be formally vacated. If Noem is reassigned to another Cabinet position, this does NOT count as leaving the Cabinet. The primary resolution source will be https://www.dhs.gov/news and https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/, with secondary confirmation from major news outlets.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly addresses the most likely candidate for first Cabinet departure according to recent reporting. If Noem leaves early in 2026 as predicted, this would strongly indicate that Trump is willing to make Cabinet changes despite his reported reluctance to admit mistakes. A 'Yes' resolution would suggest higher turnover likelihood overall, making Tulsi Gabbard's potential departure more plausible. A 'No' resolution (Noem staying through January) would indicate greater stability in Trump's Cabinet and potentially lower probability of early departures, making Tulsi Gabbard less likely to be the first to leave.

question: Will the US capture Khamenei before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. government personnel (including U.S. military, CIA, or any U.S. federal law enforcement agency) directly participate on the ground in an operation that results in the capture of Supreme Leader of Iran Ali Khamenei by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, “capture” means Khamenei is taken into physical custody and detained (including arrest, detention, or seizure) such that he is no longer free to leave at will, even if only temporarily. Voluntary surrender may qualify if it results in immediate detention/custody.

U.S. personnel must directly participate on the ground to qualify. Intelligence, surveillance, planning, logistics, transport, support, funding, training, or advisory roles alone will not count, even if they materially contribute to the operation. If U.S. personnel are physically present in the operational area and take direct action (e.g., raiding, detaining, securing, physically transferring custody), it will qualify. U.S. government contractors will be considered to be U.S. personnel if they are confirmed to be acting under the direction of U.S. government authorities.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) be designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) by the US State Department between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-26?
subquestions.background_information:
The IRGC is Iran's most powerful military and security force, directly loyal to Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and responsible for his security. The IRGC has already been designated as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT) by the US Treasury since 2019, but not as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) by the State Department. An FTO designation would represent a significant escalation in US pressure on Iran and could signal preparation for more direct action against the Iranian regime. As of February 8, 2026, the IRGC remains designated as an SDGT but not as an FTO. The State Department's FTO list currently includes groups like Hamas, Hezbollah, and Al-Qaeda, but not the IRGC. Recent tensions have increased calls for this designation, with some US lawmakers advocating for it as a response to Iran's crackdown on protests.

Sources:
- US State Department FTO List: https://www.state.gov/foreign-terrorist-organizations/
- Treasury Department SDGT List: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financial-sanctions/specially-designated-nationals-and-blocked-persons-list-sdn-human-readable-lists
- Congressional Research Service on IRGC Designations: https://crsreports.congress.gov/product/pdf/R/R46991
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the US State Department officially designates Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive). The designation must be published in the Federal Register and appear on the official State Department FTO list. The resolution will be determined using the US State Department's official Foreign Terrorist Organizations list at https://www.state.gov/foreign-terrorist-organizations/ and the Federal Register publication at https://www.federalregister.gov/. If the designation is announced but not formally published in the Federal Register by February 26, 2026, the question resolves No. If the State Department website is unavailable, the Federal Register publication will serve as the primary source.
subquestions.rationale: Designating the IRGC as an FTO would represent a significant escalation in US pressure on Iran and could indicate preparation for more direct action against the regime. Since the IRGC is directly responsible for Khamenei's security and operates as his primary protection force, such a designation could signal increased US willingness to target the regime's core security apparatus. This would be an early indicator of potential US intent to directly confront the Iranian leadership structure, making it relevant to the ultimate question about capturing Khamenei.

subquestions.rationale: TVL is a strong leading indicator for DeFi revenue generation. question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass a clean continuing resolution (CR) by November 7, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A clean continuing resolution temporarily extends government funding at previous fiscal year's levels without policy riders or earmarks. The current government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, after Congress failed to pass appropriations bills. House Speaker Mike Johnson has repeatedly brought clean CRs to the floor, but they have failed to pass due to opposition from conservative Republicans who demand spending cuts or policy changes. The House has held ten votes on clean CRs as of October 17, 2025, all failing. A clean CR passing the House would indicate reduced opposition from fiscal conservatives and increased likelihood of eventual passage, while continued failure suggests ongoing division. Current status: No clean CR has passed the House despite multiple attempts.

Sources:
- Star Local: https://example.com/star-local-shutdown-article (Note: Actual URL needed)
- House.gov: https://www.house.gov/legislative-activity
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes a clean continuing resolution (as defined: a bill that extends funding at FY2025 levels without any policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-07 23:59:59 UTC. Resolution will be determined using the official House vote records from https://clerk.house.gov/Votes and confirmed by at least two credible news sources (e.g., https://www.c-span.org/congress/bills/, https://www.nytimes.com/politics). If the House passes multiple clean CRs during this period, the first passage counts. If the data sources become unavailable, resolution will be based on consensus of credible reporting from at least three major news organizations.
subquestions.rationale: House passage of a clean CR is a crucial indicator for the ultimate question because the House has been the primary obstacle to clean CRs during this shutdown. If the House can pass a clean CR, it suggests reduced conservative opposition and increased likelihood that a clean CR will eventually become law. If the House continues to reject clean CRs through November 7th, it indicates persistent division that makes ultimate passage of a clean funding bill less likely.

question: Will Israeli troops enter Suwayda in 2025?

For the purposes of this market, aerial and maritime operations will not be considered. Only operations involving troops on the ground within Suwayda Governorate will count.

Undercover Israeli operatives and assets will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be photo and video evidence, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Israeli Defense Forces conduct at least 3 ground incursions into Syrian territory within 20km of the Suwayda border between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent reports indicate escalating Israeli ground operations in southern Syria, particularly in provinces bordering Suwayda. According to Enab Baladi (2025-09-28), Israeli forces conducted multiple ground incursions into Quneitra province in September 2025, including raids in Sida Golan, Tal al-Ahmar al-Sharqi, Jabata al-Khashab, Ofaniya, and Khan Arnaba. These operations involved military vehicles entering Syrian territory, searching homes, conducting surveys, and making arrests. The Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported these incidents, with some occurring within 20km of the Suwayda border. Israel has maintained an active military presence in southern Syria since the fall of the Assad regime in December 2023, with hundreds of strikes and ground operations documented. The current pattern shows increased frequency of ground incursions near Suwayda, potentially signaling preparation for larger operations.

Sources:
- Enab Baladi: https://english.enabbaladi.net/
- Syrian Arab News Agency: https://sana.sy/en/
- Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Israeli Defense Forces conduct at least 3 separate ground incursions into Syrian territory within 20km of the Suwayda Governorate border between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). A ground incursion is defined as: 1) IDF military vehicles crossing into Syrian territory from Israel or occupied Golan Heights, 2) Remaining in Syrian territory for at least 30 minutes, 3) Involving at least 3 military vehicles or 12 soldiers. Incursions must be reported by at least two independent credible news sources (e.g., SANA, Enab Baladi, Al Jazeera, Reuters) or officially acknowledged by IDF spokesperson. Aerial operations, maritime operations, and undercover operations do not count. If the primary sources (SANA, Enab Baladi) cease publication, secondary sources including Reuters, AFP, or AP reports will be used. The distance measurement will be based on the nearest point of the incursion location to the Suwayda Governorate border using Google Maps coordinates.
subquestions.rationale: Increased frequency of Israeli ground operations near Suwayda's borders would indicate heightened military activity and potential preparation for entry into Suwayda itself. Recent patterns show Israel conducting multiple ground incursions in neighboring provinces (Quneitra, Daraa), and escalation of this activity toward Suwayda would signal increased likelihood of Israeli troops eventually entering Suwayda Governorate. This subquestion tracks observable military patterns rather than directly asking about Suwayda entry, making it an effective leading indicator.

question: Israel x Syria security agreement by January 31?

Ceasefire announcements or other announced de-escalations such as those relating to the July 16-18 skirmishes with the Druze, or any other future military engagements, which do not address the broader security relationship will not qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Israel announce a formal withdrawal from at least two of its nine military posts in southern Syria by January 11, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: Since December 2023, Israel has maintained military presence at nine strategic posts in southern Syria, including positions on Mount Hermon and in the Syrian side of the disengagement zone. These positions include Tell al-Ahmar in Quneitra province and posts in villages such as Bir Ajam, Barikah, and Zubeida. Israel has justified this occupation as necessary for security against potential threats. Current reporting indicates these positions are a major sticking point in negotiations, with Syria demanding full withdrawal to pre-December 8, 2024 borders as a precondition for any security agreement. An Israeli withdrawal from even a subset of these positions would signal significant progress in negotiations and willingness to compromise on territorial control, which is crucial for reaching a broader security agreement. Sources: https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/11/20/Israel-s-Netanyahu-visits-occupied-Syrian-territory-as-tensions-rise, https://syrianobserver.com/news/94220.html, https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/9/netanyahu-behind-stalled-israel-syria-negotiations/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Israeli government or Ministry of Defense officially announces the withdrawal of Israeli military forces from at least two of the following nine identified positions in southern Syria: Mount Hermon (Syrian side), Tell al-Ahmar (Quneitra), Bir Ajam, Barikah, Zubeida, Ain Ziwan, Abu Qubais, and any two additional positions officially confirmed by the Israeli military as occupied posts. The announcement must occur between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive) and be verifiable through official Israeli government statements, Ministry of Defense publications, or IDF spokesperson announcements. Resolution will be based on official Israeli sources such as the Prime Minister's Office website (https://www.gov.il/en) or IDF official statements (https://www.idf.il/en). If multiple sources conflict, the most authoritative Israeli government source will prevail. Withdrawals must be explicitly announced as completed or in progress with specific timeline commitment.
subquestions.rationale: Israeli military withdrawal from occupied Syrian territory is a core Syrian demand and major obstacle to any security agreement. A partial withdrawal would demonstrate Israel's willingness to compromise on territorial control, which is essential for progress toward a broader security framework. This serves as a concrete indicator of negotiation progress rather than just diplomatic statements.

subquestions.question: Will a clean continuing resolution (CR) bill pass both chambers of Congress by November 21, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The U.S. government is currently in a shutdown that began October 1, 2025, after Congress failed to pass appropriations bills. Republicans have advocated for a 'clean' continuing resolution (CR) that extends current funding levels without policy riders, while Democrats oppose this approach and demand inclusion of healthcare provisions like ACA tax credit extensions. The House previously passed a clean CR on September 19, 2025, that would fund the government through November 21, 2025, but it failed in the Senate. A clean CR passing would indicate bipartisan cooperation and reduce immediate pressure on Trump to veto legislation, while failure suggests continued gridlock that might lead to more contentious bills reaching his desk. Current status: Government shutdown ongoing since October 1, 2025. House clean CR passed September 19, 2025; Senate rejected it. Sources: Georgia Recorder: https://georgiarecorder.com/2025/09/03/government-shutdown-warning-2025/; JD Supra: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/healthcare-preview-for-the-week-of-6982341/; Breitbart: https://www.breitbart.com/politics/2025/09/17/democrats-oppose-stopgap-spending-bill/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if both the U.S. House of Representatives and U.S. Senate pass identical versions of a clean continuing resolution (defined as a bill that extends current funding levels without substantive policy changes, amendments, or riders) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-21 (inclusive), and the bill is enrolled for presidential consideration. The resolution will be determined using congressional records from Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/) and official congressional vote records. If the bill passes both chambers but contains substantive policy changes beyond pure funding extension, the question resolves No. If the government shutdown ends through other means (e.g., full appropriations bills) before a clean CR passes, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is highly relevant because a clean CR passing would indicate reduced legislative tension and bipartisan cooperation, making it less likely that highly partisan bills (which Trump might veto) reach his desk. Conversely, if a clean CR fails, it suggests continued gridlock and increases the probability of contentious legislation being sent to Trump, raising the chance of a veto. The November 21 date aligns with the previously proposed CR end date and provides an early signal about congressional dynamics before the ultimate question's December 31 deadline.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the October 2025 CPI report (released October 15, 2025) show month-over-month core inflation at or below -0.1%?
subquestions.background_information: The Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions are heavily influenced by inflation data, particularly the Consumer Price Index (CPI). The September 2025 FOMC meeting just concluded with a 25 basis point cut, bringing the federal funds rate to 4.00-4.25%. The committee cited concerns about labor market softening while noting that inflation 'remains somewhat elevated.' Core CPI (excluding food and energy) is a key metric the Fed watches closely. The most recent data available is from August 2025, which showed core CPI at 0.3% month-over-month. A negative reading (-0.1% or lower) in the October report would represent a significant deceleration in inflation pressures and could signal to the Fed that more aggressive rate cuts are warranted, potentially influencing the 'Cut-Pause-Pause' pattern in the upcoming meetings. Sources: Federal Reserve September 2025 Statement - https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm; Bureau of Labor Statistics August 2025 CPI Report - https://www.bls.gov/cpi/; CME FedWatch Tool - https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics' October 2025 CPI report, scheduled for release on October 15, 2025 at 8:30 AM ET, shows month-over-month core CPI (Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items Less Food and Energy) at or below -0.1%. The data must be published on the official BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/cpi/) by October 16, 2025 11:59 PM ET. If the report is delayed beyond October 16, 2025, the question resolves as No. The comparison period is September 2025 to October 2025. This resolution window is from 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-16 (inclusive).
subquestions.rationale: This question is highly relevant to the ultimate 'Cut-Pause-Pause' pattern because inflation data is a primary input to Fed decision-making. A negative core CPI reading (-0.1% or lower) would represent a significant disinflationary signal that could push the Fed toward more aggressive cuts. If this subquestion resolves Yes, it increases the likelihood of cuts in October and/or December (making 'Cut-Pause-Pause' more likely). If it resolves No (inflation remains elevated), it makes pauses more likely as the Fed remains cautious about cutting too quickly amid persistent inflation pressures.

subquestions.question: Will the Canadian Consumer Price Index (CPI) annual inflation rate fall below 2.0% for any month between December 2025 and January 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The Bank of Canada's primary mandate is to maintain inflation at the 2% target midpoint. Recent CPI data shows inflation hovering around the upper end of the target range, with September 2025 CPI at 2.4% and core measures remaining sticky around 3%. The Bank has emphasized that if inflation remains near target (2%), the current policy rate of 2.25% may be appropriate. A drop below 2% would signal weakening price pressures, potentially increasing the likelihood of further rate cuts. Conversely, inflation staying above 2% would support maintaining or even raising rates. Statistics Canada releases CPI data monthly, with December 2025 data scheduled for release on January 21, 2026 and January 2026 data on February 19, 2026.

Current inflation status (September 2025): 2.4%
Bank of Canada target: 2.0%

Sources:
- https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/inflation/
- https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/251022/dq251022a-eng.htm
- https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/type/data?subject_levels=23&id=consumerpriceindex
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Resolution will be determined using:
- December 2025 CPI data (scheduled release: January 21, 2026): https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/type/release?subject=CPI
- January 2026 CPI data (scheduled release: February 19, 2026): https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/type/release?subject=CPI

If both monthly readings are at or above 2.0%, the question resolves NO. If either monthly reading is below 2.0%, the question resolves YES. If Statistics Canada fails to release either report by 2026-01-23, or revises the data in a way that changes the outcome after this date, the resolution will be based on the latest available data published by 2026-01-23. All data must come from official Statistics Canada publications.
subquestions.rationale: Inflation data is a crucial input for the Bank of Canada's rate decisions. If inflation falls below the 2% target, it would indicate weakening price pressures and potentially create room for further rate cuts. Conversely, if inflation remains at or above 2%, it would support maintaining current rates or even hiking. This subquestion provides an early indicator of whether inflationary pressures are easing sufficiently to warrant another cut in March 2026, making it a meaningful crux for the ultimate question about the Bank's March meeting decision.

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) officially announce a delay of the September 2025 Employment Situation Report (jobs report) due to a government shutdown by October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The BLS is currently facing a potential government shutdown that threatens to delay key economic data releases. According to the Department of Labor's contingency plan released on September 29, 2025, the BLS will suspend all operations during a shutdown, including data collection and publication. The September jobs report is scheduled for release on October 3, 2025, but could be delayed if a shutdown occurs. This would represent a significant disruption to the BLS's regular publication schedule and could indicate broader institutional instability. The current political standoff suggests a real possibility of shutdown-induced delays.

Sources:
- Department of Labor Contingency Plan: https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/shutdown/DOL-Contingency-Plan-FY2025.pdf
- BLS Release Calendar: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2025/release_schedule.htm
- EconoTimes Government Shutdown Threat: https://www.econotimes.com/US-Government-Shutdown-Threatens-Release-of-Key-Economic-Data-2025-09-30
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) officially announces through any of its official communication channels (website, press release, social media, or email alert) that the September 2025 Employment Situation Report will be delayed specifically due to a government shutdown, and this announcement occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15 (inclusive). The announcement must explicitly mention both the jobs report delay and the government shutdown as the reason. Temporary delays for other reasons (technical issues, data quality concerns, etc.) do not count. The primary resolution source will be the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov) and official BLS press releases. If the BLS website becomes inaccessible due to shutdown, secondary sources will include major news organizations reporting on the official BLS announcement (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator of BLS operational stability and political pressure on statistical agencies. If the BLS announces a shutdown-induced delay of its most prominent report, it suggests both immediate operational disruption and potential vulnerability to political interference. This could signal increased risk of the ultimate outcome (BLS ceasing regular publication) by demonstrating that political factors can disrupt core BLS functions. A 'Yes' outcome would indicate reduced institutional resilience, while a 'No' outcome (either no shutdown occurs or BLS maintains publication despite shutdown) would suggest greater operational stability.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States conduct at least one drone or missile strike on Syrian territory (excluding strikes on ISIS targets specifically in response to attacks on US forces) between January 13, 2026 and February 12, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The United States has maintained a military presence in Syria since 2015 as part of Operation Inherent Resolve, primarily targeting ISIS. As of January 2026, approximately 1,000 US troops remain deployed in Syria. Recent reporting indicates that US forces continue to conduct strikes against ISIS targets in Syria, with major operations occurring on December 19, 2025 (over 100 munitions fired at 70+ targets) and January 10, 2026 (over 90 bombs/missiles at 35+ targets). These strikes have been specifically framed as counter-ISIS operations in response to attacks on US personnel. However, the ultimate question concerns broader US military strikes beyond counter-terrorism operations. A strike on Syrian territory that is not specifically targeting ISIS in response to attacks on US forces could indicate a broader willingness to use military force internationally, which would be relevant for assessing the likelihood of strikes on multiple countries.

Current status: The US has conducted strikes in Syria recently, but all publicly acknowledged operations have been specifically framed as counter-ISIS measures.

Sources:
- https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-islamic-state-syria-attack-2026/ (US strikes on January 10, 2026)
- https://www.indiatvnews.com/2025/12/31/india-pakistan-conflict-2026-us-think-tank-terror-activities-2025-12-31 (mentions US troop presence in Syria)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if the United States government officially acknowledges, or credible reporting from at least two major international news organizations confirms, that US military forces conducted at least one drone or missile strike on Syrian territory between January 13, 2026 (00:00 UTC) and February 12, 2026 (23:59 UTC) that is NOT specifically described as targeting ISIS in direct response to an attack on US or coalition forces. Strikes must meet the same criteria as the ultimate question (aerial bombs, drones, or missiles impacting ground territory).

Resolution sources (in order of preference):
1. Official US government statements from Department of Defense, CENTCOM, or White House: https://www.defense.gov/News/
2. Reuters World News: https://www.reuters.com/world/
3. Associated Press International News: https://apnews.com/hub/world-news
4. BBC News World: https://www.bbc.com/news/world

If multiple sources conflict, the majority consensus of these sources will determine resolution. If the primary sources cease publication, resolution will be based on the next available source in the hierarchy. The strike must occur within the specified time window; strikes announced after February 12, 2026 but occurring before will count, while strikes occurring after February 12, 2026 will not count regardless of announcement timing.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of US willingness to conduct military strikes beyond immediate counter-terrorism responses. If the US conducts strikes in Syria that are not directly tied to protecting its forces from ISIS, it would signal a more aggressive military posture and increased likelihood of striking additional countries. Syria represents a 'baseline' country where US strikes have been routine; expansion beyond counter-ISIS operations would indicate escalation. This is particularly relevant given the recent US operation in Venezuela (Operation Absolute Resolve) and ongoing tensions with Russia/Ukraine, which could prompt broader military action. A 'yes' answer would increase the probability of the ultimate question resolving yes, while a 'no' would suggest the US is maintaining its current counter-terrorism-focused strike policy.

question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration announce any formal negotiations or working groups specifically focused on U.S.-Canada trade relations by November 30, 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Valve Corporation announce Half-Life 3 (or a differently titled continuation of the Half-Life series) with a trailer or official press release between 2025-11-10 and 2025-12-10?

Valve's last major franchise announcement was Half-Life: Alyx in November 2019, which was preceded by official press releases and trailer reveals. Sources: Tyler McVicker HLX Files Episode (https://www.youtube.com/@TylerMcVicker), Steam Events Schedule (https://store.steampowered.com/), Half-Life: Alyx Announcement History (https://www.half-life.com/en/alyx)

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly criticize Benjamin Netanyahu's handling of the Gaza ceasefire implementation by November 24, 2025?

Netanyahu has historically been defiant in his approach to Gaza operations, as evidenced by his September 2025 UN speech where he declared Israel would keep fighting terror even if Western leaders capitulated. Trump has recently claimed credit for stopping Netanyahu from continuing the war, suggesting he sees himself as the decisive force behind the ceasefire. Current tensions around implementation could prompt Trump to criticize Netanyahu if he perceives the Israeli leader as not fully implementing the agreement or undermining Trump's diplomatic victory.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Donald Trump makes any public statement (including speeches, interviews, social media posts, or press conferences) between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive) that explicitly criticizes Benjamin Netanyahu's handling of the Gaza ceasefire implementation. Resolution will be based on official White House transcripts (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), Trump's Truth Social account (https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump), or reporting from major news organizations (CNN, Fox News, AP, Reuters). Policy disagreements without personal criticism of Netanyahu do not count.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of Trump's willingness to publicly criticize Netanyahu because tensions around ceasefire implementation represent the most immediate and concrete point of potential friction between the two leaders. If Trump criticizes Netanyahu's handling of the agreement he personally brokered, it would signal deteriorating relations and increase the likelihood of broader disparagement by year-end. question: Will Russia enter Toretske by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Toretske by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Toretske is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will Russia capture any territory in Pokrovsk by December 15, 2025, as shown on the DeepStateMap?
subquestions.background_information:
Pokrovsk is a strategically important transport and logistics hub in Ukraine's Donetsk region, located approximately 50 km northwest of Toretsk. As of November 3, 2025, Russian forces have reportedly advanced into the southern part of Pokrovsk, with DeepStateMap showing Russian control of a small southern area while most of the city remains contested. Pokrovsk serves as a key logistical center with a pre-war population of around 60,000, and its capture could enable Russian advances toward Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. Recent Russian advances in Pokrovsk indicate potential momentum toward Toretsk, as successful capture of Pokrovsk would provide Russia with improved logistics and staging grounds for further operations in the Donetsk region.

Sources:
- The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/russia-says-its-forces-advance-in-embattled-ukrainian-city-of-pokrovsk
- DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/

If DeepStateMap becomes unavailable, the Institute for the Study of War map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) may be used as a secondary source. Any control gained through negotiated settlement that is reflected on these maps will count. The question resolves No if no such control is established by December 15, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: Pokrovsk serves as a critical logistical hub northwest of Toretsk, and Russian advances here would indicate both improved operational capabilities and momentum toward capturing Toretsk. Success in Pokrovsk would provide Russia with better supply routes and staging areas for attacks on Toretsk, making it a meaningful near-term indicator of Russia's ability to achieve the ultimate objective of capturing Toretsk by year-end.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) release a preliminary benchmark revision estimate for March 2026 that reduces total nonfarm employment by at least 500,000 jobs before 2025-12-30?
subquestions.background_information: The BLS conducts annual benchmark revisions to align its monthly employment estimates with more comprehensive data from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW). Recent revisions have been historically large: the preliminary benchmark for March 2025 (released September 9, 2025) reduced employment by 911,000 jobs, the largest downward revision since 2002. This pattern suggests systemic overestimation in initial reports. The preliminary benchmark for March 2024 (released August 2024) was -818,000 jobs. These revisions are critical indicators of labor market health and often precede policy responses. The BLS typically releases preliminary benchmark revisions in August or September, but the 2025 revision was delayed to September due to data processing issues. Given ongoing data quality concerns and the government shutdown mentioned in recent articles, a significant revision for March 2026 would signal severe underlying labor market weakness, increasing pressure for federal workforce reductions. Sources: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001, https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesprelbmk.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes a preliminary benchmark revision estimate for March 2026 that reduces the total nonfarm employment figure by at least 500,000 jobs (compared to the previously reported March 2026 value) during the period from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30 (inclusive). The revision must be explicitly stated in an official BLS publication, such as a press release or report titled 'Preliminary Benchmark Revision' or similar. The source for verification is the BLS website at https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesprelbmk.htm or the specific press release URL. If no such revision is published by 2025-12-30, this question resolves No. Revisions published after 2025-12-30 do not count.
subquestions.rationale: A large preliminary benchmark revision (≥500,000 jobs) would indicate severe overestimation of employment growth, revealing underlying labor market deterioration. This directly informs the likelihood of federal workforce cuts in 2025, as such revisions often prompt austerity measures or hiring freezes. The BLS's own data revisions are a leading indicator of official employment trends, and a significant downward adjustment would increase the probability of the ultimate outcome (100-150k federal employee cuts).

question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will Pakistan conduct a test launch of a ballistic missile with a range of at least 300 km between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14?

Pakistan maintains an active missile testing program, with recent tests including the Fatah-2 (400 km range) and Ababeel (2,200 km range) missiles. If multiple qualifying tests occur, the first one resolves the question YES. Resolution will be based on official Pakistan military sources at https://www.ispr.gov.pk/ and https://www.mod.gov.pk/. If these sources become unavailable, secondary sources including Reuters, Associated Press, or major international defense publications reporting the test with confirmation from Pakistani officials will be used.
subquestions.rationale: Pakistan's missile testing activity serves as a direct indicator of military readiness and potential escalation posture. subquestions.question: Will Romania invoke its peacetime drone shootdown authorization by December 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Romania has experienced repeated drone incursions into its airspace, with 13 confirmed breaches since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. On November 25, 2025, Romania scrambled NATO jets after its deepest drone incursion yet, with a drone penetrating over 100 km inland into Vrancea County. Romania has legislation (Emergency Ordinance 73/2019) allowing it to shoot down drones during peacetime if lives or property are at risk, but has not yet exercised this authority. Defence Minister Ionuț Moșteanu has stated that pilots were authorized to shoot down drones but refrained due to concerns about collateral damage. Romania shares a 650-km border with Ukraine and has been a frequent target of Russian drone activity targeting Ukrainian ports along the Danube. Sources: https://www.firstpost.com/world/romania-scrambles-nato-jets-after-deepest-ever-drone-incursion-calls-it-russian-provocatio-14181642.html, https://www.news18.com/world/nato-jets-scrambled-as-russian-drones-breach-romanian-airspace-for-the-13th-time-9238039.html, https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/nato-scrambles-jets-after-deepest-drone-breach-yet-into-romania
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Romanian government officially announces that its military forces have shot down a drone within Romanian airspace using the authority granted by Emergency Ordinance 73/2019 (or any subsequent legislation) between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-20 23:59:59 UTC. The announcement must come from an official Romanian government source (Ministry of Defence, President's Office, or Prime Minister's Office) and include confirmation that the shootdown was conducted under peacetime drone engagement protocols. If multiple drones are shot down, the first confirmed incident triggers Yes resolution. If no such announcement is made by the end date, the question resolves No. Resolution will be determined using official Romanian government statements published on their websites: https://www.mapn.ro/, https://gov.ro/, https://www.presidency.ro/
subquestions.rationale: Romania's decision to actually shoot down a drone would represent a significant escalation in NATO's response to Russian airspace violations. This would indicate increased willingness among NATO members to use kinetic force against Russian drones, which would directly increase the likelihood of NATO downing additional Russian drones (including the ultimate question). Romania has been the most frequent target of these incursions and has already authorized shootdowns in principle - actually executing one would signal a shift from defensive posturing to active engagement.
