question: Will Kamala Harris endorse Mamdani?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Kamala Harris announces that she will vote for Zohran Mamdani or endorses Mamdani for the 2025 NYC Mayor election between June 26, and November 3, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

If Kamala Harris announces that she will vote for another candidate or endorses another candidate for NYC Mayor, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Kamala Harris or one of her representatives, or a consensus of credible reporting of Kamala Harris's endorsement.

subquestions.question: Will Hakeem Jeffries publicly endorse Zohran Mamdani for NYC Mayor by September 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is a prominent Democratic leader whose endorsement would signal significant establishment support for Mamdani. As of September 1, 2025, Jeffries has not endorsed Mamdani despite meeting with him on July 18, 2025, describing their conversation as 'candid and constructive' but withholding endorsement. Jeffries' endorsement would represent a major shift from the current Democratic leadership stance where neither he, Governor Kathy Hochul, nor Senator Chuck Schumer have endorsed Mamdani. This contrasts with progressive endorsements Mamdani has received from Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and Adriano Espaillat. Jeffries' endorsement would indicate that mainstream Democratic leadership is willing to back Mamdani despite his socialist background and controversial positions, which could influence other moderate Democrats including potentially Kamala Harris.

Sources:
- https://www.yahoo.com/news/hakeem-jeffries-meets-zohran-mamdani-120000345.html
- https://www.nystateofpolitics.com/2025/07/18/rep-adriano-espaillat-endorses-mamdani-for-mayor/
- https://twitchy.com/samj/2025/06/29/how-do-you-solve-a-problem-like-mamdani-hes-a-headache-that-hakeem-jeffries-is-not-willing-to-endorse/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if Hakeem Jeffries or his official spokesperson/office publicly announces an endorsement of Zohran Mamdani for NYC Mayor between September 1, 2025 and September 20, 2025 (inclusive). The endorsement must be explicit and unambiguous, using words indicating support for Mamdani's candidacy. The announcement must appear on Jeffries' official website (https://jeffries.house.gov), official social media accounts (@RepJeffries on Twitter/X, Instagram, Facebook), or be confirmed by major news outlets citing Jeffries or his representatives. If Jeffries endorses another candidate or makes statements supporting another candidate during this period, the question resolves to 'No'. If no clear endorsement occurs by September 20, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves to 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Hakeem Jeffries' endorsement would represent a significant shift in Democratic establishment support for Mamdani. As House Minority Leader and a key party figure, Jeffries' endorsement would signal that mainstream Democrats are coalescing behind Mamdani despite his progressive/socialist background. This would create pressure on other Democratic leaders, including Kamala Harris, to also endorse the party nominee. If Jeffries endorses Mamdani, it increases the likelihood that Harris would follow suit to maintain party unity. Conversely, if Jeffries continues withholding endorsement, it suggests ongoing establishment reluctance that might also influence Harris' decision.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 12 launch by November 30?
description:
If the 12th SpaceX Starship successfully launches from its launch pad by November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Yes”. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The outcome of any launch will be corroborated by examining official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

Any subsequent anomaly (e.g., an explosion) after the launch will have no bearing on the outcome. Any name change of the Starship with another vehicle will have no bearing on the outcome of the market.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX conduct a successful static fire test of a Super Heavy booster designated for Flight Test 12 at Starbase between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17?
subquestions.background_information:
Static fire tests are a critical pre-launch milestone for SpaceX's Starship program. They involve firing the booster's engines while the vehicle is secured to the launch mount, verifying engine performance, avionics, and ground support equipment. A successful static fire is typically one of the final steps before a launch attempt and indicates that the vehicle has passed major pre-flight checkouts. The Super Heavy booster for Flight Test 12 (likely Booster 16 or similar designation) would need to undergo this test. The most recent Flight Test 11 launched on October 13, 2025, following a successful static fire test. SpaceX typically conducts these tests at its Starbase facility in Boca Chica, Texas, and announces them via official channels like X (formerly Twitter).

Sources:
- SpaceX X account for test announcements: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
- NASA Spaceflight coverage of Starship testing: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/tag/starship/
- NSF Forum for community tracking: https://forum.nasaspaceflight.com/index.php?board=72.0
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if SpaceX publicly announces (via its official X account @SpaceX) the successful completion of a static fire test for a Super Heavy booster that is explicitly designated for use in Flight Test 12, occurring between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17 (inclusive). A 'successful' test is defined as one where SpaceX's announcement indicates all engines fired as intended for the full duration planned, with no major anomalies requiring investigation that would delay the launch campaign. If SpaceX announces a test but does not confirm it as successful (e.g., 'test conducted, data review ongoing'), the question does NOT resolve Yes based on that announcement. If the designated booster for Flight Test 12 changes after a static fire test (e.g., due to an issue), only tests of the booster that ultimately is used for Flight Test 12 count. The primary source for resolution is SpaceX's official X account (https://twitter.com/SpaceX). Secondary sources like NASA Spaceflight (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/) or the NSF Forum (https://forum.nasaspaceflight.com/) may be used to corroborate the test occurred if SpaceX's announcement is ambiguous, but the official SpaceX announcement is definitive for 'success' determination.
subquestions.rationale: A successful static fire test is a strong leading indicator that SpaceX is progressing smoothly toward Flight Test 12. It demonstrates that the hardware (booster) is functional and that ground systems are ready, reducing the risk of last-minute technical delays. Given the historical cadence (e.g., Flight 11's static fire was a few weeks before launch), a Yes answer by mid-November would signal a high likelihood of meeting the November 30 launch date. Conversely, a No answer (no test or an unsuccessful test) by November 17 would indicate potential delays, as there might be insufficient time to resolve issues and launch by the end of November.

question: Will Khamenei visit Russia by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ali Khamenei visits Russia by June 30, 2026, 11:59PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "visit" is defined as Ali Khamenei physically entering the terrestrial territory of Russia in a voluntary capacity. Whether or not Ali Khamenei enters Russian airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

Entering Russia requires physically entering sovereign Russian territory, including all Russian federal subjects and territories. Areas under Russian control but not under Russian sovereignty (e.g., Crimea) do not count. Russian airspace, Russian embassies/consulates abroad, and international zones do not constitute Russian sovereign territory.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Russia and Iran announce a new bilateral security or military cooperation agreement by February 9, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent developments suggest deepening security ties between Russia and Iran. In October 2025, Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Ali Larijani visited Moscow carrying a personal letter from Ayatollah Khamenei, signaling enhanced strategic cooperation. Reports from January 2026 indicate Russian military transport planes making frequent flights to Tehran, potentially transporting weapons and removing gold amid Iran's domestic unrest. There are also reports of potential Iranian purchases of Russian fighter jets. These developments suggest ongoing security coordination that could culminate in formal agreements. A new security or military cooperation agreement would indicate continued strengthening of ties and could facilitate arrangements for potential leadership relocation. Current status: No new comprehensive security/military agreements have been announced between Russia and Iran since their strategic partnership treaty signed in January 2025.

Sources:
- RT World News: https://www.rt.com/news/594567-russia-iran-security-cooperation/
- Хартия 97: https://charter97.org/en/news/2026/1/9/587856/
- Tehran Times: https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/496789/Larijani-and-Putin-discuss-economic-regional-and-international
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Russia and Iran officially announce a new bilateral security cooperation agreement, military cooperation pact, or defense treaty between 2026-01-10 and 2026-02-09 (inclusive). The announcement must be made through official government channels (press releases, statements from presidential offices, ministry websites, or official news agencies). The agreement must represent new substantive cooperation beyond existing arrangements and must include specific military or security provisions (weapons transfers, joint exercises, intelligence sharing, military technology transfer, etc.). The announcement must be verifiable through official Russian government sources (http://kremlin.ru/, http://government.ru/) or Iranian government sources (http://president.ir/, http://www.mfa.ir/). If no such announcement is made by 2026-02-09, the question resolves NO.
subquestions.rationale: A new security or military cooperation agreement between Russia and Iran would indicate deepening strategic ties and potentially facilitate arrangements for Khamenei's potential relocation to Russia. Such an agreement would signal Russia's willingness to provide security guarantees and infrastructure that could support a high-profile political exile, making a Khamenei visit more likely. This serves as an early indicator of political alignment that could precede an actual visit.

question: Will Han Duck-soo be sentenced to prison before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo is sentenced to any time in jail/prison for charges related to the 2024 South Korean political crisis, including but not limited to allegations of failure to promulgate legislation, obstruction of constitutional processes, or other criminal acts stemming from his actions as Acting President and Prime Minister by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will remain open through 2026 regardless of whether Han Duck-soo's initial sentencing includes prison.  Any sentencing will qualify, regardless of subsequent appeals or changes to the sentence.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the South Korean government and law enforcement; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will South Korean prosecutors formally request an arrest warrant for Han Duck-soo between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25?
subquestions.background_information:
Han Duck-soo is currently on trial for charges including abetting insurrection, perjury, and falsifying official documents related to the December 2024 martial law crisis. On August 24, 2025, prosecutors initially sought an arrest warrant for Han, but the Seoul Central District Court dismissed the request, citing insufficient evidence of flight risk or evidence tampering. However, prosecutors proceeded with indicting Han on August 29, 2025, without detention. The trial began on September 30, 2025, and is ongoing. A formal arrest warrant request would indicate prosecutors believe there is new evidence or increased risk that justifies detention during trial, which could signal increased likelihood of conviction and potential prison sentence. Historically, arrest warrants for high-profile political figures in South Korea (like former presidents Park Geun-hye and Lee Myung-bak) have often preceded convictions and prison sentences.

Sources:
- https://www.bssnews.net/news/130623 (Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha)
- https://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20250829000742 (The Korea Herald)
- https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/south-korea-ex-pm-hans-martial-law-trial-begins (The Straits Times)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if South Korean prosecutors (including the Special Prosecutor's Office or any official prosecutorial body with jurisdiction) formally file a request for an arrest warrant against Han Duck-soo with a court between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25 (inclusive). The request must be publicly announced through official channels (press conference, official statement, or court filing) and reported by at least two credible news sources. Resolution will be based on the earliest date of public announcement or court filing.

Primary resolution source: Official statements from the Supreme Prosecutors' Office of Korea (https://www.spo.go.kr/eng/) or Seoul Central District Court (https://www.scourt.go.kr/eng/).

Secondary resolution sources: Reporting from at least two of the following credible news organizations: Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr/), The Korea Herald (https://www.koreaherald.com/), The Korea Times (https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/), or JoongAng Daily (https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/).

If prosecutors withdraw the request before the court rules on it, the question still resolves Yes based on the initial filing. If the request is made but not publicly reported until after 2025-12-25, the question resolves based on the date of the official filing.
subquestions.rationale: A formal arrest warrant request would indicate prosecutors have gathered substantial new evidence or believe Han poses a flight risk, signaling increased legal pressure and likelihood of conviction. This would be a strong early indicator of potential prison sentencing, as arrest warrants for high-ranking officials in South Korea's political corruption cases have historically correlated with eventual convictions and imprisonment.

question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

subquestions.question: Will the total U.S. crude oil inventories (excluding Strategic Petroleum Reserve) fall below 430 million barrels at any weekly report between December 27, 2025 and January 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
U.S. crude oil inventories are a key indicator of oil market supply-demand balance. Lower inventories typically signal tighter supply relative to demand, which can support higher oil prices. The Energy Information Administration (EIA) releases weekly inventory data every Wednesday at 10:30 AM EST. As of December 19, 2025, U.S. commercial crude oil inventories stood at 448.1 million barrels (Source: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report). The 430 million barrel threshold represents a significant decline from current levels and would indicate substantial inventory drawdowns. Historically, inventory levels below this threshold have often coincided with periods of higher oil prices due to supply constraints.

Sources:
- EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report: https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Commercial Crude Oil Inventories (excluding Strategic Petroleum Reserve) reported by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) in any Weekly Petroleum Status Report published between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26 (inclusive) falls below 430 million barrels. The resolution will be based on the 'U.S. Commercial Crude Oil Inventories (Excluding SPR)' figure as published in the EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report available at: https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/. If the EIA fails to publish a report during this period, or if multiple reports are published for the same week, the first published official report will be used. If no official EIA report is published during this period, the question will resolve as No.
subquestions.rationale: Significant inventory drawdowns below 430 million barrels would indicate tightening supply conditions in the U.S. market, which historically correlates with upward pressure on crude oil prices. This early indicator of supply-demand balance could provide valuable insight into whether market fundamentals support a move toward $70/bbl by June 2026. The weekly frequency and public availability of EIA data make this a timely and objective indicator.

question: David Baszucki out as Roblox CEO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if David Baszucki ceases to be CEO of Roblox for any length of time between August 14, and December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of David Baszucki's resignation/firing before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/firing goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from Roblox and/or David Baszucki, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Roblox Corporation announce any major child safety policy changes (e.g., mandatory ID verification for all users, expanded moderation tools, or partnerships with external safety organizations) by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Roblox is currently facing significant public pressure and legal scrutiny regarding child safety on its platform. A petition calling for CEO David Baszucki's resignation has garnered over 250,000 signatures, citing concerns about inadequate protection of young users from predators. The Louisiana Attorney General has filed a lawsuit alleging that Roblox permits 'an online environment in which child predators thrive.' Current Roblox safety measures include automated moderation systems and human review, but critics argue these are insufficient. Recent controversies include the banning of a 'predator hunter' YouTuber and allegations that predators remain on the platform for extended periods despite reports. Sources: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/esports/roblox/roblox-communitys-push-for-ceo-david-baszuckis-exit-hits-over-250000-signatures-amidst-rising-controversies/articleshow/117123123.cms, https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/396263/thousands-of-roblox-users-urge-ceo-to-quit.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Roblox Corporation publicly announces (via official blog post, press release, SEC filing, or official social media account) at least one major child safety policy change between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). Major changes include: 1) Implementation of mandatory ID verification for all users (not just age 17+), 2) Significant expansion of moderation tools or staffing (e.g., doubling moderation team size), 3) Partnership with established child safety organizations (e.g., NCMEC, Thorn), 4) Implementation of new parental control features beyond current options. Resolution will be determined using Roblox's official blog (https://blog.roblox.com), SEC filings (https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search), or official Twitter account (@roblox).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator of whether Roblox leadership (including Baszucki) is responding substantively to the child safety crisis. If Roblox announces major safety improvements during October 2025, it suggests the company is taking external pressure seriously and attempting to address concerns proactively, which might reduce pressure for Baszucki's removal. Conversely, if no meaningful safety changes are announced despite mounting pressure, it could indicate leadership intransigence or inability to address core issues, potentially increasing the likelihood of Baszucki's eventual departure. The October 2025 timeframe provides an early signal before the ultimate question's resolution period.

question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt reaches the listed value this year at any point by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury report a federal budget deficit of at least $1.9 trillion for fiscal year 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal budget deficit is a primary driver of national debt growth. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) reported on September 9, 2025 that the U.S. had accumulated a $2 trillion deficit over the first 11 months of fiscal year 2025 (October 2024 through August 2025), with total FY2025 spending of $6.7 trillion and revenues of $4.7 trillion. The CBO projected the total deficit for FY2025 would be $1.8 trillion. However, actual deficits often differ from projections, and the final FY2025 deficit figure will be a crucial indicator of whether the national debt continues accelerating toward $38 trillion. The Treasury Department typically releases the final monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) for September, which concludes FY2025, within a few weeks after the fiscal year ends on September 30.

Sources:
- KPVI: https://www.kpvi.com/news/national_news/report-u-s-racked-up-2-trillion-deficit-over-past-11-months/article_8a5d3a4c-6d5f-11ef-bf8c-7b4d4f5c3c7c.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the U.S. Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement for September 2025 (the final month of fiscal year 2025) reports a total federal budget deficit of $1.9 trillion or greater for fiscal year 2025 (October 1, 2024 - September 30, 2025). The deficit figure must be published on the Treasury Department's official website between October 1, 2025 and October 19, 2025 (inclusive). If the Treasury Department does not publish the September 2025 MTS by October 19, 2025, this question resolves as NO. The official source is the Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement publication: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/monthly-treasury-statement/.
subquestions.rationale: The federal budget deficit directly contributes to national debt accumulation. A deficit of $1.9 trillion or higher would indicate continued rapid debt growth, making it more likely the $38 trillion threshold will be reached in 2025. Given the CBO's projection of a $1.8 trillion deficit and the reported $2 trillion deficit through August, this threshold represents a meaningful acceleration beyond projections. The resolution timing (mid-October) aligns with when the Treasury typically releases final FY2025 data, providing an early indicator of debt trajectory before year-end.

question: Will CME self certify a sports contract in 2025?
description:
This market resolves to “Yes” if CME Group files a self-certification under CFTC Regulation 40.2 for at least one sport-based event contract by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it resolves to “No.”

For this market, “self-certify” means CME, acting as a DCM or self-listing exchange, submits a written certification per 17 C.F.R. § 40.2 that the contract complies with the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations. The contract must explicitly reference a sporting event (e.g. game result, player performance, etc.). Announcements alone do not qualify; the filing must be made and publicly verifiable.

The resolution source will be the CFTC’s public filings, CME’s disclosures, and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Polymarket (via QCEX) launch trading of at least one sports-based event contract (as defined by CFTC Regulation 40.2) by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Polymarket acquired CFTC-registered designated contract market QCEX in July 2025 for $112 million to re-enter the US market. On October 1, 2025, Polymarket/QCEX submitted self-certification filings to the CFTC for sports-based contracts including 'athletic event,' 'athletic spread,' and 'total score' outcomes, effectively enabling moneyline, point spread, and total betting on sporting events. These contracts were scheduled to be listed 'no earlier than October 2, 2025.' Polymarket's return to the US market with sports contracts would represent direct competition to CME and could indicate regulatory acceptance of sports-based event contracts. Currently, Kalshi is the only exchange actively trading sports event contracts, while CME has partnered with FanDuel but has not yet self-certified any sports contracts. The legal status of these contracts remains contested by multiple state gambling regulators who argue they constitute illegal sports betting.

Sources:
- https://www.covers.com/news/polymarket-preparing-sports-betting-included-return-to-us
- https://finance.yahoo.com/news/kalshi-self-certifies-wide-array-130000782.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Polymarket (trading as QCEX) launches trading of at least one sports-based event contract on its exchange platform between 2025-10-09 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). A sports-based event contract is defined as any contract that references the outcome of a sporting event (e.g., game result, player performance, point spread, or total score) as described in CFTC Regulation 40.2. Resolution will be determined by:

1. Verification of active trading on Polymarket/QCEX's official trading platform (https://polymarket.com/ or https://qcex.com/)
2. Confirmation through the CFTC's public filings database (https://sirt.cftc.gov/sirt/sirt.aspx?Topic=SelfCertifiedRuleSubmissions)
3. Secondary verification through credible financial news reporting

If Polymarket/QCEX announces but does not actually launch trading of sports contracts during this period, the question resolves No. If the launch is delayed beyond October 31, 2025, the question resolves No. The primary resolution source will be the CFTC's self-certification database, with secondary verification from Polymarket/QCEX's official website and trading platform.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is highly relevant because Polymarket/QCEX's successful launch of sports contracts would indicate continued regulatory acceptance of sports-based event contracts by the CFTC and market demand for such products. If a major competitor like Polymarket successfully launches sports contracts, it could create competitive pressure on CME to enter this market space. Conversely, if Polymarket fails to launch despite its filings, it could signal regulatory obstacles or market conditions that might also deter CME. The outcome of this question would provide valuable information about the regulatory environment and market readiness for sports event contracts just before CME's potential decision window.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 Superheavy explode?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the booster for the eleventh Starship-SuperHeavy test explodes at any point during the test from the start of fueling operations to 60 minutes after it makes contact with Earth upon landing. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An explosion is defined as a violent and catastrophic event resulting in the destruction of all or part of the vehicle, regardless of intent or context (e.g., a planned termination event would also count).

If the eleventh launch has not occurred by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: The sixth Starship-SuperHeavy test flight which exploded after executing controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico would qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX publicly acknowledge a significant hardware modification to Starship's Super Heavy booster landing system before October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX's Starship program has experienced multiple failures during landing operations, including explosions during Flight Test 9 (May 2025) and Flight Test 10 (August 2025). Recent tests have focused on improving landing reliability, with Flight 10 demonstrating intentional shutdown of one engine during descent and using backup engines for landing burn. SpaceX has been implementing hardware changes to address landing failures, including modifications to engine configurations and landing procedures. Any significant hardware modification announced before the next flight could indicate continued concerns about landing reliability and potentially increase the risk of explosion during Flight Test 11. Current landing success rate for Super Heavy boosters is approximately 20% across all test flights, with the most recent landing attempt (Flight 10) resulting in a controlled explosion.

Sources:
- https://www.theregister.com/2025/08/27/spacex_starship_flight_10/
- https://www.theregister.com/2025/08/18/spacex_tenth_starship_flight_test/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if SpaceX officially announces any hardware modification specifically targeting the Super Heavy booster landing system (including but not limited to engine configuration changes, landing leg modifications, structural reinforcements, or propellant management systems) through any of the following channels: SpaceX's official Twitter/X account (@SpaceX), official press releases on spacex.com, or statements from Elon Musk's verified Twitter/X account (@elonmusk). The announcement must occur between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive) and must explicitly reference changes to improve landing reliability or address landing-related failures. Minor procedural changes or software updates alone do not qualify - the modification must involve physical hardware changes. If multiple announcements occur, the first qualifying announcement determines resolution.

Primary resolution source: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
Secondary sources: https://www.spacex.com/, https://twitter.com/elonmusk
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of SpaceX's confidence in their current landing system design. If SpaceX announces significant hardware modifications to the Super Heavy booster landing system before Flight Test 11, it suggests they identified ongoing reliability issues that could increase the probability of explosion during the next test. Conversely, no modifications would indicate confidence in current systems. This provides valuable information about potential risk factors for Flight Test 11's outcome without directly asking about the explosion itself.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI release a Windows version of ChatGPT Atlas in public beta or general availability by November 22, 2025?

question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will the EU formally approve the use of frozen Russian central bank assets for Ukraine's reconstruction, with disbursement approval by the European Commission or Council, by November 12, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The European Union has been debating the use of frozen Russian assets to support Ukraine's reconstruction efforts. Approximately €260 billion of Russian Central Bank assets were frozen by Western countries following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, with about €210 billion held in the EU. Recent discussions have focused on using windfall profits from these assets or the assets themselves for Ukraine's defense and reconstruction. The European Parliament has previously called for utilizing these assets, and there have been ongoing negotiations among EU member states about the legal and political feasibility of such actions. As of October 2025, no formal EU-wide approval for direct asset transfer has been implemented, though some countries have expressed support while others have raised legal concerns. This development would signal increased Western commitment to Ukraine's long-term security and reconstruction, potentially affecting future negotiations with Russia including buffer zone discussions.

Sources:
- European Parliament resolution on Russian assets: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-9-2024-0001_EN.html
- EU frozen Russian assets overview: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/eu-response-ukraine-invasion/frozen-assets/
- Current debate on asset utilization: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/eu-debates-using-frozen-russian-assets-fund-ukraines-reconstruction-2024-01-15/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the European Commission formally approves the use of frozen Russian central bank assets for Ukraine's reconstruction OR the European Council adopts a formal decision approving such use, with the approval occurring between 2025-10-13 and 2025-11-12 (inclusive). The approval must be documented in an official EU legal instrument (regulation, decision, or directive) published in the Official Journal of the European Union or through an official press release from the European Commission or Council. The approval must specifically authorize the disbursement of funds from frozen Russian assets (not just windfall profits) for Ukraine's reconstruction. If multiple approvals occur, the first qualifying approval within the resolution window determines the outcome. The resolution will be based on official EU publications at https://eur-lex.europa.eu/ and https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en.
subquestions.rationale: EU approval of using frozen Russian assets for Ukraine's reconstruction would signal a significant escalation in Western commitment to Ukraine's long-term security and reconstruction efforts. This would demonstrate reduced concern about potential Russian retaliation and increased willingness to take concrete actions that undermine Russia's financial position. Such a move would likely harden negotiating positions on both sides, making a buffer zone agreement less likely as it would indicate the EU is prioritizing long-term support for Ukraine over seeking negotiated settlements with Russia. The timing of this decision within the next month would provide an important indicator of European resolve ahead of potential winter negotiations.

subquestions.question: Will the December 2025 Federal Funds Rate futures contract (ZQZ25) close at or above 95.00 (implying a 5.00% rate or lower) on any trading day between November 17, 2025 and December 5, 2025?

This would signal strong market conviction in imminent monetary easing, which typically puts downward pressure on longer-term Treasury yields like the 10-year. Current market pricing shows uncertainty about December rate cuts, with probabilities fluctuating between 50-70% according to recent reports. The December contract is actively traded on CME Group, with real-time pricing widely available.

- Federal Reserve Rates: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly probes market expectations for Federal Reserve policy easing, which is a primary driver of Treasury yields. The December 5th cutoff ensures this indicator resolves well before the ultimate question's end date while allowing time for the Fed's policy signal to influence yield movements. question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Violations over Ukraine or international waters do not count. The primary resolution source will be NATO's official website (https://www.nato.int) and official government defense ministry websites. If official sources provide conflicting counts, the NATO official count will take precedence.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tracks Russia's direct testing of NATO airspace boundaries, which serves as an early indicator of escalating tensions and potential willingness to conduct strikes on NATO territory. Multiple airspace violations in a short timeframe would demonstrate increased Russian aggression and risk-taking behavior near NATO borders, potentially signaling preparation for or testing of more direct military actions. subquestions.question: Will the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) report at least one confirmed Russian advance of ≥1 km toward Drobysheve from any direction between January 30, 2026 and February 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Drobysheve is a strategically located village in Donetsk Oblast, currently contested between Russian and Ukrainian forces. According to recent reports from January 27-28, 2026, Russian forces claim to have captured over 90% of Drobysheve's residential areas as part of their Donbas offensive operations. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) provides daily, detailed assessments of territorial control in Ukraine, though they have been critical of Russian claims, noting exaggeration of gains. For example, ISW disputed Russian claims about capturing Kupyansk-Uzlovaya and questioned the scale of reported territorial gains. Recent Russian advances in the area have been characterized by infiltration tactics and street fighting, particularly in nearby Krasny Liman and Ilyichevka. The current frontline positions around Drobysheve show Russian forces making gradual progress but facing determined Ukrainian resistance.

Sources:
- https://www.pravdareport.com/world/178998-russian_forces_take_settlements/
- https://charter97.org/en/news/2026/1/28/587751/
- https://www.understandingwar.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) publishes at least one daily assessment between January 30, 2026 and February 26, 2026 (inclusive) that explicitly reports a confirmed Russian territorial advance of ≥1 kilometer toward Drobysheve from any direction. The advance must be specifically mentioned in the ISW text assessment and must represent ground gained in the direction of Drobysheve (within a 45-degree arc centered on Drobysheve from the reported advance location). 

Resolution will be based on the text assessments published on ISW's official website (https://www.understandingwar.org/). The measurement of ≥1 km must be either explicitly stated by ISW or clearly measurable using the accompanying maps and geographic references provided. If ISW uses terms like 'advanced approximately 1 km' or 'gained over 1 kilometer' in the direction of Drobysheve, this qualifies. Minor advances (<1 km) or advances in other directions do not count.

If ISW ceases publication during this period, the question will resolve as NO. If ISW reports are ambiguous or contradictory, the most recent assessment before February 26, 2026 will be used. The resolution will be determined based on the timestamp of the ISW publication (Eastern Time).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator of Russian momentum toward capturing Drobysheve. A confirmed advance of ≥1 km reported by ISW (which tends to be conservative in its assessments) would signal that Russian forces are making meaningful progress toward the ultimate objective. Given that Russian forces currently claim control over 90% of Drobysheve but ISW has been skeptical of such claims, a verified advance would indicate both actual military progress and ISW's confirmation of that progress. This provides a more reliable indicator than Russian military claims alone and addresses the vulnerability of map-based resolution by focusing on text-based assessments from a reputable source.

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Russian President Vladimir Putin publicly acknowledge Ukraine's sovereignty over any currently occupied territories (excluding Crimea) by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent reports indicate Russia maintains maximalist territorial demands in Ukraine, including claims beyond current occupied areas to regions like Odesa and Mykolaiv. Putin has repeatedly invoked historical claims to southern Ukraine and rejected Western peace proposals. However, diplomatic signals from Russia could indicate potential flexibility in negotiations. As of October 2025, Russia occupies approximately 18% of Ukraine's territory including Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson regions. Any acknowledgment of Ukrainian sovereignty would represent a significant shift in Russia's negotiating position and could indicate willingness to accept territorial compromises.

Sources:
- https://telanganatoday.com/russia-has-provided-fresh-evidence-of-its-territorial-ambitions-in-ukraine
- https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-which-territorial-concessions-are-being-discussed/a-70479321
- https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraine-may-cede-russianheld-territory-in-peace-plan--telegraph-3890848
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Russian President Vladimir Putin or the Russian Foreign Ministry (through official statements, interviews, or diplomatic communications) explicitly acknowledges Ukraine's sovereignty over any portion of territory currently occupied by Russian forces (excluding Crimea) between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive). The acknowledgment must be clear, unambiguous, and publicly verifiable through official Russian government channels or credible media reporting. Statements must specifically reference Ukrainian sovereignty or territorial integrity regarding occupied regions. Resolution will be based on official Kremlin statements (http://kremlin.ru), Russian Foreign Ministry statements (http://mid.ru), or credible international media reports citing official Russian sources. If conflicting statements occur, the most recent official position from Putin or the Foreign Ministry will determine resolution.
subquestions.rationale: This question serves as an early indicator of Russia's negotiating flexibility. If Putin acknowledges Ukrainian sovereignty over occupied territories (even partially), it suggests Russia may be willing to accept territorial compromises rather than demanding complete Ukrainian capitulation. This would increase the likelihood of Ukraine agreeing to a deal that involves some territorial concessions while preserving Ukrainian sovereignty claims. Conversely, continued Russian maximalist positions would indicate low probability of Ukraine accepting any territorial deal under current conditions.

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the data for the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2025 shows the second greatest increase of any previously recorded year when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An anomaly which is the second greatest of any previously recorded year for 2025 is necessary and sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes" immediately once the data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for 2024 and/or 2025 is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2025" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will NOAA's November 2025 Arctic sea ice extent average be at least 1.5 million km² below the 1981-2010 average?
subquestions.background_information:
Arctic sea ice extent serves as a sensitive indicator of global warming trends, with lower ice extent correlating with higher global temperatures. According to NOAA's December 2025 Arctic Report Card, the Arctic experienced its lowest maximum sea ice extent in the 47-year satellite record during the 2024-2025 period, with continued warming trends. The current November 2025 Arctic sea ice extent is approximately 8.5 million km², which is about 1.2 million km² below the 1981-2010 average of 9.7 million km². This threshold of 1.5 million km² below average would represent a significant departure from historical norms and could indicate stronger than expected warming patterns that might contribute to 2025 ranking as the second hottest year on record.

Sources:
- NOAA Arctic Report Card 2025: https://arctic.noaa.gov/report-card/
- NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice News & Analysis: https://nsidc.org/arcticseaicenews/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if NOAA's National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) reports that the November 2025 monthly average Arctic sea ice extent was at least 1.5 million km² below the 1981-2010 November average. The data must be published between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive) on the NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice News & Analysis page (https://nsidc.org/arcticseaicenews/). If NSIDC does not publish November 2025 data by 2026-01-11, this question will resolve based on the first authoritative publication of this data from any of the following sources: NASA Earth Observatory, NOAA Climate.gov, or Copernicus Climate Change Service, in that order of preference. If no authoritative source publishes this data by 2026-01-11, the question will resolve as No.
subquestions.rationale: Arctic sea ice extent is a strong indicator of global temperature trends due to polar amplification, where the Arctic warms faster than the global average. A particularly low November 2025 sea ice extent (1.5 million km² below average) would suggest accelerated warming patterns that could contribute to 2025 ranking as the second hottest year on record. This subquestion provides an early indicator before the final 2025 global temperature data is released, as sea ice data is typically published earlier than comprehensive global temperature datasets.

question: Will Trump talk to Nicolás Maduro by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if President of Venezuela Nicolás Maduro talks with Donald Trump between October 15 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

A talk is defined as any interaction between the listed individual and Donald Trump, occurring either in person or through verbal communication by phone or video call.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez participate in any public diplomatic meeting or official communication with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio between 2025-11-15 and 2025-11-25?
subquestions.background_information: High-level diplomatic engagement between Venezuelan and U.S. officials would be a significant indicator of potential normalization efforts. Currently, U.S.-Venezuela relations are severely strained, with the U.S. conducting military strikes against Venezuelan targets and not recognizing Maduro's government. Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez is Maduro's top diplomatic representative and key political ally. Recent reports indicate minimal diplomatic contact between the two governments, with Rodríguez publicly denying negotiation attempts (Dawn, 2025-10-19). Any public meeting or official communication between Rodríguez and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio would represent a notable shift in diplomatic posture and could signal preparations for higher-level engagement, including potential Trump-Maduro talks.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio participate in any publicly acknowledged diplomatic meeting (in person or virtual) or engage in official communication (phone call, video conference, or publicly released correspondence) between 2025-11-15 00:00 UTC and 2025-11-25 23:59 UTC. The communication must be confirmed by official statements from either government or credible reporting from at least two major news organizations. If the event is postponed beyond November 25, 2025, it resolves No. Resolution will be based on official government statements (U.S. State Department: https://www.state.gov, Venezuelan government: https://www.vicepresidencia.gob.ve) and credible news sources including Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), and BBC (https://www.bbc.com).
subquestions.rationale: High-level diplomatic engagement between Venezuelan and U.S. officials would indicate a thaw in relations and potential preparation for direct talks between Trump and Maduro. As Maduro's closest political ally and top diplomat, Rodríguez's engagement with Rubio would signal serious diplomatic intent from Venezuela and willingness from the U.S. to engage at senior levels, making direct Trump-Maduro communication more likely.

question: Trump invokes War Powers against Iran by March 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the Trump Administration submits a 48-hour report consistent with the War Powers Resolution regarding the introduction of U.S. armed forces into hostilities or imminent hostilities against Iran between the date of market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The market will resolve based on the listed date of the report. This market may stay open until 10 days after the listed date (ET) to allow for a qualifying report to be published.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be the White House, the Congressional Record, and the NYU Law War Powers Resolution Reporting Project; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the House of Representatives vote on a War Powers Resolution specifically targeting Iran by February 28, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: Congressional War Powers Resolutions have been a key mechanism used by lawmakers to challenge President Trump's military actions. Following the Venezuela military operation in January 2026, Democrats have signaled intentions to introduce War Powers Resolutions targeting multiple countries including Iran. A House vote on such a resolution would indicate serious congressional pushback against potential military action against Iran and could signal increased political pressure on the administration. The House previously voted on a Venezuela War Powers resolution on January 22-23, 2026, which ended in a 215-215 tie (defeating the measure). Current political dynamics show some Republican defections on war powers issues, with Representatives Thomas Massie (R-KY) and Don Bacon (R-NE) supporting the Venezuela resolution. Sources: Washington Examiner (https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/), Common Dreams (https://www.commondreams.org/), CBS News (https://www.cbsnews.com/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the U.S. House of Representatives holds a recorded vote on a War Powers Resolution (concurrent resolution or similar legislative vehicle) that specifically addresses military action against Iran between 2026-02-13 and 2026-02-28 (inclusive). The resolution must explicitly mention Iran in its text or title and seek to limit or require congressional authorization for military action against Iran. Resolution will be determined based on official House floor proceedings recorded in the Congressional Record (https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record) or official House vote records. If multiple votes occur, the first qualifying vote determines resolution. If the vote is postponed beyond February 28, 2026, the question resolves NO.
subquestions.rationale: A House vote on an Iran-specific War Powers Resolution would indicate significant congressional opposition to military action against Iran, potentially constraining the administration's options. This could reduce the likelihood of Trump invoking War Powers against Iran by creating political pressure and potentially forcing the administration to seek congressional authorization. The Venezuela precedent shows that such resolutions can extract commitments from the administration regarding military actions.

question: OpenAI social app in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a social iOS app owned by OpenAI is available for installation on the US iOS app store by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

subquestions.question: Will Elon Musk's xAI file a motion for a preliminary injunction against Apple and OpenAI in their Texas antitrust lawsuit by September 27, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 25-26, 2025, Elon Musk's xAI filed a federal antitrust lawsuit in Texas against Apple and OpenAI, alleging collusion to block competition in the AI market. The lawsuit claims Apple's partnership with OpenAI creates an unfair advantage for ChatGPT while suppressing competitors like xAI's Grok. A preliminary injunction would be a significant escalation in this legal battle, indicating xAI is seeking immediate court intervention to change Apple's App Store practices. This would signal serious legal pressure on Apple's relationship with OpenAI and potentially impact App Store policies regarding AI app distribution. The current status shows no preliminary injunction has been filed yet, but Musk has threatened immediate legal action.

Sources:
- Elon Musk Sues Apple and OpenAI Over Alleged App Store Bias: https://www.macobserver.com/news/elon-musk-sues-apple-openai-app-store-bias/
- xAI Sues Apple and OpenAI for Alleged Market Collusion: https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/xai-sues-apple-openai-market-collusion/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Elon Musk's xAI files a motion for preliminary injunction in their antitrust lawsuit against Apple Inc. and OpenAI LP (Case No. 1:25-cv-00842, U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-27 (inclusive). The motion must be filed with the court and appear on the official court docket accessible via PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/). Resolution will be based on the official court filing date. If the case is transferred to another district or the case number changes, resolution will be based on filings in the active case. If no motion is filed by September 27, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This legal escalation would indicate significant pressure on Apple's App Store policies and its relationship with OpenAI. If xAI seeks immediate court intervention through a preliminary injunction, it suggests they believe Apple's practices are actively harming competition, which could influence Apple's willingness to approve or feature competing AI social apps like a potential OpenAI social app. A preliminary injunction filing would represent a serious legal threat that could affect App Store review processes and partnerships during the critical period when OpenAI might be preparing to launch a social app.

question: Will Google Gemini 3 score at least 40% on Humanity’s Last Exam by January 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Humanity’s Last Exam leaderboard lists any Google Gemini 3 model with a score of at least the specified score by the specified January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will Google release a new Gemini 3 technical report or performance update (including any score on Humanity's Last Exam) by December 5, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Google typically releases technical reports or official performance updates when launching new AI models or making significant improvements to existing ones. These reports provide detailed benchmark results, including scores on tests like Humanity's Last Exam (HLE). Currently, the latest publicly known Gemini model is Gemini 2.5 Deep Think, which scored 34.8% on HLE as of August 2025. A new technical report or update from Google specifically mentioning Gemini 3 and providing any performance data (even if preliminary) would be a strong indicator of progress toward the ultimate goal of Gemini 3 achieving 40% on HLE by January 2026. This would signal that Google is actively developing and testing Gemini 3, and is confident enough to share performance metrics publicly.

Sources:
- Gemini 2.5 Deep Think HLE score: https://www.extremetech.com/computing/google-gemini-2-5-deep-think-uses-multiple-ai-agents-to-tackle-a-single-problem
- Previous Gemini 2.5 Pro HLE score: https://dev.to/tech_enthusiast/exploring-gemini-25-pro-a-look-at-googles-latest-ai-model-4p5a
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The update must include at least one benchmark score (including but not limited to Humanity's Last Exam) for Gemini 3. If multiple updates occur, the first one meeting these criteria will trigger resolution. If no such update occurs by 2025-12-05, the question resolves No.

Primary source for resolution: Google's official AI blog (https://blog.google/technology/ai/) or Google DeepMind's official website (https://deepmind.google/). Secondary source: Official Google or Google DeepMind Twitter/X account (@Google, @GoogleDeepMind).
subquestions.rationale: A new technical report or performance update from Google specifically about Gemini 3 would indicate active development progress and confidence in the model's capabilities. If Google releases such a report (even with preliminary scores), it suggests they are on track for potential improvements leading to the 40% HLE target. Conversely, if no update is released by early December, it may indicate delays or less confidence in Gemini 3's near-term performance, making the ultimate 40% goal less likely.

question: Ukraine agrees not to join NATO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ukraine publicly agrees not to join NATO by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An official pledge by Ukraine not to join NATO will qualify for a “Yes” resolution whether as a unilateral announcement or part of an agreement with the Russian Federation. 

Any agreement or pledge made before the resolution date of this market will qualify, regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO for any amount of time will count (e.g. If Ukraine not to join NATO for 10 years this will qualify).

An agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995 “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement is an example of a qualifying agreement. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by the Ukraine, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming a qualifying agreement has been reached will also count.

subquestions.question: Will the European Parliament adopt a resolution explicitly rejecting Ukraine's NATO membership ban by December 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The European Parliament has consistently supported Ukraine's sovereignty and NATO aspirations. On November 25, 2025, the Parliament adopted a resolution (B10-0546/2025) that rejected the US-Russia peace plan requiring Ukraine to constitutionally ban NATO membership, calling it 'capitulation' that 'rewards aggression'. The resolution endorsed an alternative proposal allowing NATO membership by consensus. The Parliament has historically been vocal about Ukraine's right to choose its alliances, and its position could significantly influence Ukraine's negotiation stance. The current Parliament session runs until December 18, 2025, with potential for additional resolutions before the holiday recess. Sources: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/B-10-2025-0546_EN.html, https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20251121IPR18328/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the European Parliament adopts a resolution between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-20 (inclusive) that explicitly rejects or condemns any requirement for Ukraine to ban or limit NATO membership aspirations. The resolution must be published on the official European Parliament website and contain clear language opposing restrictions on Ukraine's alliance choices. Resolution will be determined using the official European Parliament legislative database: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/. If no such resolution is adopted by December 20, 2025, the question resolves NO.
subquestions.rationale: The European Parliament's position on Ukraine's NATO membership is a crucial indicator of Western support for Ukrainian sovereignty. If the Parliament strongly rejects NATO membership bans, it signals continued Western backing for Ukraine's alliance choices, making Ukrainian concessions less likely. Conversely, if the Parliament doesn't take a strong stance, it could indicate weakening Western resolve and increased pressure on Ukraine to accept restrictions, making a 'no NATO' agreement more probable.

question: Will a new country join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any country not already a part of the Abraham Accords formally signs a normalization agreement with Israel under the framework of the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

Countries already part of the Abraham Accords as of June 26, 2025—including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan—will not count.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Saudi Arabia announce a formal peace proposal that includes recognition of Israel and a Palestinian state before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia has consistently maintained that normalization with Israel is contingent upon a clear path to a Palestinian state, as outlined in the Arab Peace Initiative. Recent polls show 81% of Saudis view normalization negatively since the Gaza war began. However, diplomatic efforts continue, with Trump recently expressing hope for Saudi Arabia to join the Abraham Accords. A formal peace proposal announcement would represent a significant shift in Saudi policy and could indicate movement toward eventual normalization. Current status: No formal peace proposal including recognition of Israel has been announced by Saudi Arabia as of October 2025.

Sources:
- https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/17/trump-expects-expansion-of-abraham-accords-soon-hopes-saudi-arabia-will-join
- https://www.washingtoninstitute.org/policy-analysis/saudi-attitudes-toward-israel-normalization-august-2024
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Saudi Arabia's government officially announces a comprehensive peace proposal that includes both recognition of Israel's right to exist and the establishment of a sovereign Palestinian state with defined borders between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). The announcement must come from an official government source (royal decree, foreign ministry statement, or official spokesperson) and be reported by at least two major international news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, or BBC). The proposal must explicitly mention both Israeli recognition and Palestinian statehood as integrated components. If the proposal is announced but later retracted within the resolution window, it still counts as Yes. The resolution source will be official Saudi government statements and major international news coverage. If conflicting reports emerge, resolution will be based on the most authoritative government source.

Primary source: https://www.spa.gov.sa/
Secondary sources: https://www.reuters.com/, https://apnews.com/
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia's position is widely seen as the most significant potential expansion of the Abraham Accords. A formal peace proposal announcement would represent a major diplomatic breakthrough and indicate Saudi leadership is seriously considering normalization with Israel, which would be a strong precursor to actually joining the Abraham Accords. This subquestion captures near-term diplomatic momentum that would significantly increase the probability of a new country joining the accords in 2025.

question: Another France debt downgrade by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if France's long-term sovereign credit letter rating is downgraded by any of the three major credit rating agencies (S&P, Moody's, Fitch) at any point between September 12, 6:15 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Standard & Poor's, Moody's, or Fitch; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will France's 10-year government bond yield exceed 3.60% on at least 5 trading days between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13?
subquestions.background_information: France's sovereign debt yields have risen significantly amid political uncertainty and fiscal concerns. Following Fitch's downgrade from AA- to A+ on September 12, 2025, the 10-year yield reached 3.47%, close to Italy's level. Historically, credit rating downgrades typically lead to higher borrowing costs as investors demand higher risk premiums. The current yield of 3.47% represents a significant increase from previous levels, and breaching the 3.60% threshold would indicate sustained market pressure on French debt. This could signal deteriorating investor confidence that might precede further rating downgrades by Moody's or S&P, both of which have scheduled reviews in the coming months. Sources: Investing.com, AFP, Bloomberg
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if France's 10-year government bond yield closes at or above 3.60% on at least 5 separate trading days between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13 (inclusive). The yield data will be sourced from Bloomberg's French Government Bond Yields page (https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/rates-bonds/government-bonds/france) using the daily closing yield for the 10-year maturity. If Bloomberg data is unavailable, the European Central Bank's Statistical Data Warehouse (https://sdw.ecb.europa.eu/) will serve as the backup source. Weekend and non-trading days are excluded. If market data is unavailable for 5 consecutive trading days due to extraordinary circumstances, the question will resolve based on the most recent available data.
subquestions.rationale: Sovereign bond yields are a direct reflection of market confidence in a country's creditworthiness. A sustained increase in France's 10-year yield above 3.60% would indicate deteriorating investor sentiment regarding France's fiscal stability, potentially foreshadowing further credit rating downgrades. This subquestion provides an early market-based indicator that could predict whether Moody's or S&P will follow Fitch's recent downgrade, making it highly relevant to the ultimate question about additional France debt downgrades.

question: Will Donald Trump visit North Korea in 2025?
description:
If U.S. President Donald Trump visits North Korea between August 4 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will North Korea officially confirm through state media that Kim Jong-un will attend the 2025 APEC summit in South Korea between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit is scheduled to be held in South Korea in late October 2025.
